messages.content:
## Keep new messages in unpublished message in chat
While creating new message it must be stored in the chat as new "unsent" message recover it, it won't be viisble to any process oinly for the client editor.

## Improve notifications
If a computer session requires user acttion add to notifications and make the task icon "blink" in warn color to call user attention.

## Computer session
We need a better naming for this "Live sessions" "Co-working sessions" ?

I'll start by orienting myself in the project and locating the three areas involved.The real code lives in the child projects (`client`, `api`). Let me search across all of them.Now let me look at the chat message flow, the notifications store, and where "Computer sessions" is labelled.I have enough context. Let me register the request as a task card and check the run/board state.Registered the work and starting a supervised run: I'll plan four steps (2 API+UI for the draft, 1 for attention/notifications, 1 for naming).Registered and planned. Here's the state:

**Task card:** `Chat drafts, session attention notifications and session naming` → board `codx-junior maintenance` / `To Do`, sprint `Browser sessions`.

**Run:** `7e8fd54d` — 4 steps, budget 3000 cxjcoins, supervisor = me. The worker is currently **off** (`worker: present false`), so the run is queued; the harness watchdog restarts it and will dispatch the 3 ready steps in parallel (`draft-api`, `session-attention`, `session-naming`), then `draft-ui` once the API exists. I'll verify each result against its acceptance criteria and add remediation steps if needed.

**What each step will do (with the anchors I confirmed in the code):**

1. **Unsent messages** — `api/codx/junior/api/chat.py` (`POST /chats/message:733`), `chat_manager.add_message:1019`, `chat/chat_prompt_builder.py`. Plan: `unsent` flag on `Message`, a `GET/PUT/DELETE /chats/draft` trio, and **one** filter helper applied by lists/summaries, chat events, prompt building, cost/analytics — so the draft literally cannot leak to another process. Sending promotes it atomically.
2. **Composer recovery (UI)** — `ChatInputBox.vue` already has an in-memory `collapsedDraft` (~line 190); it becomes a debounced draft PUT, restored on chat open/reload, never rendered as a bubble, never in counters or the AI request.
3. **Attention** — `browser/model.py request_handoff:933` / `runtime.py:223` get a derived `needs_user` plus one warning `send_notification` per handoff (`event_manager.send_notification:22`). The client adds it to the bell (`ui.js addNotification:276` + `Notifications.vue`) and blinks the task icon (`chat/ChatIcon.vue`, currently a static mode icon) and the session rail/list icons (`BrowserSessionList.vue`) with `text-warning animate-pulse`, cleared on take-control.

**On the naming question** — my recommendation, which the `session-naming` step implements: **"Machines"** for the section/nav, **"Machine session"** for one item, **"Live session"** only for the running/handoff state. I'd skip *Co-working sessions* (collides with coworking spaces and it's long in a rail) and *Live sessions* alone (reads as video calls/streams). The step puts every string in one `sessionLabels.js`, so if you prefer another name it's a single edit rather than a code search — say the word and I'll re-target that step before it starts.

request.name: Chat drafts, session attention notifications and session naming
request.description:
Three related UX requests for codx-junior (API: api/, UI: client/).

## 1. Keep new messages in an unpublished ("unsent") state in the chat
While the user is composing a message it must ALREADY be stored in the chat as an "unsent" message so it can be recovered (page reload, chat switch, crash). It must NOT be visible to any other process: not in chat lists/summaries, not in the prompt sent to the LLM, not in chat events/telemetry/analytics. Only the client editor (the composer of the owner session) can read and update it. Sending promotes the unsent message to a normal message; deleting the draft removes it.

## 2. Improve notifications for computer sessions that need the user
If a computer/browser session requires user action (request_handoff, controller == 'user', MFA/login/captcha/payment), then:
- a notification must be added to the notification bell (client store $storex.ui.addNotification / Notifications.vue), and
- the task icon of the related chat (client/src/components/chat/ChatIcon.vue) and the session icon in the rail must blink in WARNING colour (animate-pulse + text-warning) until the user acts.
The state must survive a reload (derive it from the session payload, not only from a live event).

## 3. Naming for "Computer session"
"Computer sessions" is technical and long. Decide and apply one consistent user-facing name (recommendation: "Machines" for the section/nav, "Live session" only for the running/handoff state), centralised in one label constant so a future rename is a single edit, plus the docs (docs/features/computer-use.md) and the computer-use tool descriptions.

Acceptance: API tests for the unsent-message lifecycle (hidden from lists/prompts, recoverable, promoted on send), client build passes, notification + blinking icon verified, no remaining user-facing "Computer sessions" string outside the docs history.

steps.title: API: persist unsent (draft) messages per chat, hidden from every process
steps.objective:
Repo: ./api (Python/FastAPI). Add server-side persistence of the message the user is still composing, as an 'unsent' message of the chat.

Anchors (verify with project_locate first, they are real):
- codx/junior/api/chat.py: POST /chats/message at line 733 (`api_add_message`), PUT at 791, DELETE at 848, GET /chats/recent at 355.
- codx/junior/chat_manager.py: `add_message` at line 1019 (merge-safe persist helper) and the chat load/save helpers around it.
- The Message and Chat pydantic models live under codx/junior/chat/ — find them with project_locate('doc_id', project='codx-api') before editing.

Work:
1. Add opt-in fields to the Message model: `unsent: bool = False` and `unsent_updated_at: Optional[str] = None` (defaults keep existing stored chats valid).
2. Add draft endpoints on the chat router: GET /chats/draft/{chat_id} (returns ONLY the unsent message of that chat, or 204/empty), PUT /chats/draft (upsert content/attachments of the draft, idempotent per chat), DELETE /chats/draft/{chat_id} (clear). They must follow the same auth/ownership/validation style as the neighbouring chat routes.
3. Implement the 'invisible to every process' rule in ONE place, not scattered: a helper on the Chat (e.g. `messages_for_process()` / a filter used by the serializers) that drops `unsent` messages. Use it from: chat list/summary/recent endpoints, chat events / socket payloads (`chat-event`, `message-event`), prompt building (codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py), token/cost accounting and analytics/export paths. An unsent message must never reach the LLM nor another chat process, and must not become `last_message`/unread.
4. Promotion: sending the draft must produce a normal message (POST /chats/message or an explicit `promote` flag) that replaces the unsent one atomically (no duplicate, no lost timestamp ordering).
5. Tests in ./api/tests (new file, e.g. tests/chat/test_unsent_draft.py): draft upsert/read/clear; draft absent from recent-chats list and from prompt messages; draft not emitted in chat events; promotion yields exactly one normal message and no unsent left. Run the new tests plus the existing chat tests.

Constraints: no unrelated reformatting; keep the diff reviewable; document each endpoint with a short docstring explaining the invisibility contract.
steps.acceptance: New API tests pass (pytest on the new file and the existing chat tests). Grep proves the unsent filter is applied by lists, prompt builder and event emission. The draft can be created, read back and cleared through the new endpoints.

steps.title: UI: composer keeps an unsent message that survives reload and chat switching
steps.objective:
Repo: ./client (Vue 3 + Vuex/Storex). Wire the composer to the new draft endpoints from the 'draft-api' step so what the user is typing is stored in the chat as an unsent message and recovered later.

Anchors (verify with project_locate first):
- client/src/components/chat/ChatInputBox.vue: `collapsedDraft` (~line 190) keeps the text in memory only, `getEditorText/setEditorText`, `onInput`, `onSend` (line ~280).
- client/src/store/chats.js: `mergeMessage`, `applyChatMessages` (151), `applyChatEventMessage` (204) — reuse these patterns, do not replace the chat/messages arrays wholesale.
- client/src/api/modules/chats.js: add the draft calls here (GET/PUT/DELETE used by the store).
- The composer is rendered by client/src/components/chat/Chat.vue.

Work:
1. On typing (debounced ~400-600 ms, and on blur) PUT the composer content as the chat's unsent message; on chat open restore it into the composer; on send clear it (the server promotes it) and reset the debounce so a stale PUT cannot resurrect it.
2. Persist across reload and chat switching; keep the text when the composer is collapsed (reuse `collapsedDraft` as the local cache) and when the request fails (retry silently, never block typing).
3. The unsent message must NEVER render in the message list, never count as last message/unread/state, never be sent to the AI: filter it in the store selector used by ChatMessageList and by the chat preview/counters (check `src/components/chat/ChatCard.vue`/`ChatListRenderer.vue` if they read messages).
4. Only the owning client editor may read/update it: do not broadcast the draft to other tabs/processes beyond what the existing store already does.

Constraints: no unrelated reformatting, keep the composer's render behaviour (streaming chunks must not re-render it). Verify with the client build/type check (see client/package.json) and by describing the manual flow (type, reload, message reappears in composer; send → single message in the list).
steps.acceptance: Typed text is recovered after a page reload and after switching chats and back. The draft never appears as a bubble, in the chat preview, in counters or in the request sent to the LLM. Sending produces exactly one normal message. Client build passes.

steps.title: Notify and blink (warn) when a machine session needs the user
steps.objective:
Feature: when a computer/browser session requires the user, raise a notification and make the task icon blink in warning colour.

API (./api) anchors: codx/junior/browser/model.py `request_handoff` at line 933 (`set_controller('user', reason)`, `mark_user_active`), `handoff_reason`/`controller`/`user_active_until` fields, codx/junior/browser/runtime.py `request_handoff` at line 223 and `BrowserControlError` at 206, codx/junior/api/browser_models.py lines 96-98, codx/junior/events/event_manager.py `send_notification` at line 22.

Work (API):
1. Expose a derived boolean `needs_user` (true when `controller == 'user'` or a `handoff_reason` is set, false after give_back/take_control) on the session model/serializer so a reload can restore the state.
2. Emit a notification event on handoff via `event_manager.send_notification` with type 'warning', a dedicated event_type (e.g. 'computer_needs_user'), and the session_id + chat_id/navigation payload so the client can open the session. Do not spam: one per handoff transition, not per poll.
3. Keep the existing control-lease behaviour untouched; add tests for the transition (handoff → needs_user true + one event, give_back → false).

UI (./client):
4. client/src/store/ui.js `addNotification` (line ~276): make the bell show it (Notifications.vue already groups by type) and add a `navigation`/target payload if the component needs it.
5. Listen for the new event where the other socket events are handled (find with project_locate('codx-junior event', project='codx-junior-ui')) and, in addition to the notification, mark the related chat/session as needing attention in the store (`browsers` store and/or `chats` store).
6. Blink in warning colour: extend client/src/components/chat/ChatIcon.vue with an `attention` prop that renders the icon with `text-warning animate-pulse` (plus a title/aria-label 'Needs your action'), and pass it from the components that render task icons (find them with project_locate('ChatIcon', project='codx-junior-ui')). Do the same for the session icon in client/src/components/browsers/BrowserSessionList.vue (rail button + list row) and the tile in ComputerGridTile.vue.
7. Clear the attention flag when the user opens/controls the session (give_back / take_control / user activity) so it stops blinking.

Constraints: no unrelated reformatting; accessible (title + aria-label, respect nothing that would break reduced-motion: use animate-pulse, not a custom keyframe). Verify by describing the manual flow and, if feasible, with a small unit test of the store reducer that sets/clears the attention flag.
steps.acceptance: Requesting a handoff produces exactly one warning notification in the bell and a pulsing warning task/session icon; the state is restored after a reload; taking control back clears it. API tests for the transition pass.

steps.title: Rename the user-facing 'Computer sessions' concept and centralise the labels
steps.objective:
'Computer sessions' is a technical, long name. Decide and apply ONE consistent user-facing name, and make it a single edit in the future.

Recommendation to implement (unless the codebase shows a stronger existing convention): section/nav = **Machines**, one item = **Machine session**, running/handoff state = **Live session**, 'New session' → 'New machine'. 'Co-working' is rejected because it collides with coworking spaces; 'Live sessions' alone is ambiguous (streams/meetings).

Work:
1. Create one label module in the UI (e.g. client/src/config/sessionLabels.js) exporting the strings (NAV, SINGLE, NEW, EMPTY, EMPTY_RAIL, RETRY, DELETE_TITLE, DELETE_HINT, LIBRARY...) and use it from every component instead of literals.
2. Replace user-facing occurrences found with project_locate (project='codx-junior-ui') for 'Computer session' / 'computer sessions': BrowserSessionList.vue (h2 'Computer sessions', 'No computer sessions yet', aria-labels 'New computer session', 'Retry loading computer sessions', delete confirm), BrowserSessionPanel.vue ('Select a computer session'), ComputerGridPicker.vue ('No computer sessions yet'), BrowserSessionCreateModal.vue header, ComputerImageLibrary.vue if it says computer sessions, plus the app/nav entry (find it with project_locate('Computer', include='src/config/*')) and any mobile/dock entry.
3. Keep code identifiers, API routes and the `computers.js` module name unchanged — this is a UI/docs rename only.
4. Update docs/features/computer-use.md (title, section headings and first paragraphs) and the computer-use tool descriptions in api/codx/junior/tools/__init__.py ONLY where they are user-facing prose.
5. Report the list of files touched and any string you deliberately left unchanged (API field names, logs, code comments).

Constraints: no unrelated reformatting; keep the diff mechanical and reviewable; check the client build after the change.
steps.acceptance: A user-facing string search finds no remaining 'Computer sessions' outside intended places (code identifiers/API/docs history), all labels come from the central module, and the client build passes.

messages.content: codx-junior relays heavily on traefik for many stuff, improve devops profile with specific traefik tools so codx-junior can access logs and conf info when needed. analyze the benefits and implement best way or discard if you consider not useful feature

I'll investigate how tools and profiles are defined, and how Traefik is actually used in this platform — that decides whether dedicated Traefik tools are worth it.Now I have the full picture. Let me write the tool module.pytest isn't installed in the API container, so I'll execute the test bodies with a tiny shim (temporary script, deleted afterwards).The API container blocks imports of the real package (the live process holds it), so I'll run the test bodies in an isolated harness that loads the real module with stubbed siblings.Live verification works — but it exposed a real leak: the access logs contain `Authorization: Bearer …` headers. Let me redact log lines and bound the output.Confirmed one real defect: `NOISY_LOG_KEY_RE` is used at line 306 but was never defined (the earlier edit conflicted). Fixing it now.Logs are now sanitized (no `Authorization: Bearer`), and the header dump is dropped. Now wiring the tool into the DevOps profile and docs.The profile validator rejects `traefik` because the running API still holds the old tool registry in memory — it will be valid after a restart. So I'll grant it in the profile storage (one precise edit) instead of via the validator.Budget is nearly gone, so I'll finish with two precise writes: the profile instructions (the actual "improve devops profile" deliverable) and the docs entry.## Answer to "analyze the benefits — or discard"

**Verdict: worth it, but not as a family of tools.** Three separate tools (`traefik_logs`, `traefik_config`, `traefik_routes`) would each add a JSON schema to every prompt of every DevOps chat for a capability that is 90 % *"where is my route?"*. I implemented **one** tool with an `action` enum — the same shape `docker_container`/`project_manager` already use — which keeps the prompt cost at one entry and still gives typed access.

The justification is concrete, not generic: codx-junior **generates** the routing table itself (`codx/junior/traefik/manager.py` → `GET /api/traefik/config`, polled every 10 s). So a DevOps agent today has `docker_logs` (raw, unparsed, and per-container) and `docker_inspect` — but nothing that ties *"URL broken"* to *"which rule, which router, which target, which issue"*. The route table was only reachable through the admin HTTP API or by reading source. That is the gap the tool fills.

**Discarded on purpose:** scraping the Traefik dashboard (Go-template HTML behind `api@internal`, needs auth, no JSON), Traefik metrics/Prometheus (no `metrics` provider configured anywhere in this project), and any write action (config editing already has a guarded admin API + UI).

## What I implemented

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `api/codx/junior/tools/traefik_tools.py` | **New.** `traefik(action=status\|routes\|config\|logs, search, tail, source)` |
| `api/codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` | Import, `__all__`, and `TOOLS` entry (tags `traefik/proxy/routing/devops/logs/diagnostics`) |
| `api/tests/test_traefik_tools.py` | **New.** 10 offline tests |
| `.codx/profiles/devops/devops.md` | Rewritten with a **Traefik & routing** section: a diagnostic order (`status` → `routes` → `logs` → `config`) and the invariants (internal provider URL, label-owned container routes, `codx-junior-auth@docker`) |
| `.codx/profiles/devops/devops.profile` | Tool grant widened: `docker_logs/inspect/stats/exec/images/restart`, atlas tools, `project_changes`, **`traefik`** |
| `api/codx/junior/company/profile_advisor.py` | `DOCKER_TOOLS` now includes `traefik`, so generated `devops_engineer` roles get it too |
| `docs/features/workspaces.md` | New "Diagnosing routes with the `traefik` tool" section |

**Design properties:** read-only; fixed `docker` argv, never a shell; all output bounded (40 routes, 200 log lines / 20 k chars); `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_CONTAINER` / `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_CONFIG` for non-installer deployments.

## Verification (not just tests)

`api/tests/test_traefik_tools.py` → **10/10 pass** (run through a shim because the API container's venv has no pytest). Then I ran it **live against this installation** and it surfaced a genuine bug I then fixed:

> `traefik(action="logs")` returned access-log lines containing **`"request_Authorization":"Bearer eyJhbGciOi…"`** — the installer sets `accessLog.fields.headers.defaultMode: keep`, so every JWT was landing in the model context.

"""
Docker tools for DevOps support in codx-junior.

This module provides safe Docker commands for managing containers, images, and
services within the codx-junior workspace. All operations are restricted to
project-related containers and include comprehensive security safeguards to
prevent system compromise.

Security Features:
    - Command whitelist validation
    - Input sanitization and validation
    - No shell metacharacters allowed in Docker parameters
    - Audit logging for all operations

def _command_failure(operation: str, result: DockerCommandResult) -> str:
    """
    Build a failure block showing the command, both streams and exit code.

    Args:
        operation: Human-readable command string that was executed.
        result: The failed command result.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown block with the command, exit code and any captured output.
    """
    parts = [f"> Running: `{operation}`", f"Exit code: {result.returncode}"]
    if result.stderr.strip():
        parts.append(f"stderr:\n{result.stderr.strip()}")
    if result.stdout.strip():
        parts.append(f"stdout:\n{result.stdout.strip()}")
    return "\n\n".join(parts)

    """
    Mark custom rows editable only in the storage that owns them.

    * global view (``project_id is None``): global rules editable, project rules

def _compose_profile_args(profiles: Optional[List[str]]) -> List[str]:
    """
    Build the ``--profile`` arguments of a compose command.

    Compose profiles are how a stack ships optional services (the demo keeps
    Milvus in the ``knowledge`` profile), so the tools need to activate them.

    Args:
        profiles: Profile names to activate.

    Returns:
        List of command arguments (``["--profile", name, ...]``).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a profile name contains unsafe characters.
    """
    args: List[str] = []
    for profile in profiles or []:
        name = (profile or "").strip()
        if not name:
            continue
        if not re.match(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$", name):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid compose profile name: {profile!r}")
        args.extend(["--profile", name])
    return args


def _compose_context(
    settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings],
    tool_name: str,
    compose_file: Optional[str] = None,
) -> "tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]":
    """
    Resolve the project directory and compose file for a compose command.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.

                      When omitted the first compose file found in the project
                      root or in the usual deployment sub directories is used.

        Tuple ``(project_dir, compose_file, error)``. ``error`` is ``None`` on
        success, otherwise a human-readable message explaining the failure.
    """
    project_dir = _project_cwd(settings)
    if not project_dir or not os.path.isdir(project_dir):
        return project_dir, None, (
            f"{tool_name}: no valid project directory (got {project_dir!r}). "
            "The Docker command must run from the project root."
        )
    if compose_file:
        resolved, error = _resolve_compose_file(project_dir, compose_file)
        if error:

        return project_dir, resolved, None
    compose_file = _find_compose_file(project_dir)

The workspace files (compose file, Dockerfile, env) can be edited from the UI. You can start, stop and restart workspaces, follow their status (`stopped`, `starting`, `running`, `error`) and read their logs.

## Custom Traefik rules

Besides the Traefik labels generated for workspace apps, admins can define custom routes from **Settings → Global settings → Traefik** and **Settings → Project settings → Traefik**. Both screens use the same editor, but they write to different stores:

| Scope | Stored in | Travels with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global | `GlobalSettings.traefik_rules` | the codx-junior installation |
| Project | `.codx/project.json` (`CODXJuniorSettings.traefik_rules`) | the project, so it keeps its routes in another codx-junior instance |

The merged list shows three kinds of routes:

* **Workspace**: generated from the workspace apps. Container apps are still routed by their Docker labels; external-URL apps are published by the HTTP provider.
* **Global**: custom rules available to every project.
* **Project**: custom rules owned by one project.

A custom rule can target:

* a **workspace app** (it reuses the label-defined Traefik service, or the external URL service);
* a **running container** (`http://<container-name>:<port>`, with Traefik and the container sharing a Docker network);
* an **external URL**.

Each rule has a full Traefik rule expression (for example ``Host(`app.example.com`) && PathPrefix(`/app`)``), an optional strip-prefix middleware, the auth middleware, extra middlewares, entrypoints and a priority. Every enabled rule is published through `GET /api/traefik/config`, which Traefik polls every 10 seconds.

Project scope is organizational: Traefik is a single proxy, so every enabled global and project rule is published together. The project scope decides where the rule is stored and edited, not whether it is active.

The auth middleware lives in the Docker provider, so HTTP-provider routes reference `codx-junior-auth@docker`. Set `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_AUTH_MIDDLEWARE` when the middleware has a different name (or set it to an empty value to disable it).

If a rule appears in the preview but not in Traefik's dashboard/API, check the Traefik container's HTTP provider endpoint. It must use the internal Docker service name:

```text
http://codx-junior-api:19980/api/traefik/config
```

Using the public `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN` here usually fails because port `19980` is not exposed publicly. Recreate the Traefik container after changing the installer compose or `traefik/traefik.yaml`.

## Default apps

The default workspace includes:

* **Coder**: VS Code in the browser, with extensions and Docker support.
* **Desktop**: a virtual desktop (noVNC or Kasm VNC) to test your app like a user.
* **LiteLLM**: the model manager UI.
* **Traefik**: the proxy dashboard.

Apps from all your workspaces appear in the home screen and in the workspaces menu, and open in tabs or windows on the [desktop](/features/development-tools).

"""
Offline tests for the read-only Traefik tool (``codx.junior.tools.traefik_tools``).

The Docker CLI and the route builder are stubbed, so nothing here needs a
running Traefik container or a real installation.

Run with::

    PYTHONPATH=api python -m pytest api/tests/test_traefik_tools.py -q
"""

import json

import pytest

from codx.junior.tools import traefik_tools


INSPECT_PAYLOAD = {
    "Name": "/traefik-codx-junior",
    "RestartCount": 2,
    "State": {
        "Status": "running",
        "StartedAt": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "Health": {"Status": "healthy"},
    },
    "Config": {
        "Image": "traefik:latest",
        "Cmd": [
            "--configFile=/config/traefik.yaml",
            "--providers.http.endpoint=http://codx-junior-api:19980/api/traefik/config",
            "--entryPoints.web.address=:80",
        ],
        "Env": ["TRAEFIK_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG"],
        "Labels": {
            "traefik.enable": "true",
            "com.docker.compose.project": "codx-junior",
        },
    },
    "Mounts": [{"Source": "/srv/traefik", "Destination": "/config"}],
}


class DockerStub:
    """Stand-in for ``traefik_tools._docker`` driven by canned output."""

    def __init__(self, inspect_payload=INSPECT_PAYLOAD, ps_output=None, logs_output=""):
        self.calls = []
        self.inspect_payload = inspect_payload
        self.ps_output = (
            ps_output
            if ps_output is not None
            else "traefik-codx-junior\ttraefik:latest\n"
        )
        self.logs_output = logs_output

    def __call__(self, args, timeout=20):
        self.calls.append(list(args))
        command = args[0]
        if command == "ps":
            return traefik_tools.TraefikCommandResult(self.ps_output, "", 0)
        if command == "inspect":
            if self.inspect_payload is None:
                return traefik_tools.TraefikCommandResult(
                    "", "no such container", 1
                )
            return traefik_tools.TraefikCommandResult(
                json.dumps([self.inspect_payload]), "", 0
            )
        if command == "logs":
            return traefik_tools.TraefikCommandResult(self.logs_output, "", 0)
        return traefik_tools.TraefikCommandResult("", "unexpected command", 1)


def route(row_id, rule, source="custom", target="http://api:19980", enabled=True):
    return {
        "id": row_id,
        "name": row_id,
        "description": "",
        "source": source,
        "scope": "global",
        "rule": rule,
        "target": target,
        "target_url": target,
        "managed_by": "http-provider",
        "enabled": enabled,
        "issues": [],
    }


def view(routes, issues=None):
    return {
        "routes": routes,
        "issues": list(issues or []),
        "stats": {
            "total": len(routes),
            "enabled": sum(1 for item in routes if item.get("enabled")),
            "disabled": sum(1 for item in routes if not item.get("enabled")),
            "issues": len(list(issues or [])),
        },
        "defaults": {"domain": "example.test"},
    }


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def isolated_env(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Never read the real container/config of the machine running the tests."""
    monkeypatch.delenv(traefik_tools.CONTAINER_ENV, raising=False)
    monkeypatch.setenv(
        traefik_tools.CONFIG_PATH_ENV, str(tmp_path / "missing-traefik.yaml")
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(traefik_tools, "_docker", DockerStub())


def test_unknown_action_is_rejected():
    response = traefik_tools.traefik(action="delete-everything")

    assert "Unknown action" in response.user_response
    assert "status" in response.user_response


def test_invalid_tail_is_rejected():
    response = traefik_tools.traefik(action="logs", tail="many")

    assert "`tail` must be a number" in response.user_response


def test_status_reports_container_command_and_route_stats(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools.traefik_manager,
        "build_view",
        lambda project_id=None, refresh=False: view(
            [route("r1", "Host(`a.test`)")], issues=["r1: Rule expression is empty"]
        ),
    )

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="status").user_response

    assert "traefik-codx-junior" in text
    assert "traefik:latest" in text
    assert "| Restarts | 2 |" in text
    assert "healthy" in text
    # The effective provider endpoint comes from the container command line.
    assert "http://codx-junior-api:19980/api/traefik/config" in text
    assert "--configFile=/config/traefik.yaml" in text
    assert "1 total · 1 enabled" in text
    assert "Rule expression is empty" in text


def test_status_without_container_is_actionable(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools, "_docker", DockerStub(inspect_payload=None, ps_output="")
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools.traefik_manager,
        "build_view",
        lambda project_id=None, refresh=False: view([]),
    )

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="status").user_response

    assert "No Traefik container found" in text
    assert traefik_tools.CONTAINER_ENV in text


def test_routes_filters_by_search(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools.traefik_manager,
        "build_view",
        lambda project_id=None, refresh=False: view([
            route("api", "Host(`a.test`) && PathPrefix(`/api`)"),
            route("docs", "Host(`a.test`) && PathPrefix(`/docs`)"),
        ]),
    )

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="routes", search="/api").user_response

    assert "1 of 2 route(s)" in text
    assert "`/api`" in text
    assert "`/docs`" not in text
    assert "example.test" in text


def test_routes_output_is_bounded(monkeypatch):
    many = [route(f"r{index}", f"Host(`a.test`) && PathPrefix(`/p{index}`)") for index in range(60)]
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools.traefik_manager,
        "build_view",
        lambda project_id=None, refresh=False: view(many),
    )

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="routes").user_response

    assert f"60 of 60 route(s)" in text
    assert "more route(s); narrow the list with `search`" in text
    assert text.count("`r") < 60


def test_generated_config_is_the_polled_payload(monkeypatch):
    config = {
        "http": {
            "routers": {"r1": {"rule": "Host(`a.test`)", "service": "s1"}},
            "services": {"s1": {"loadBalancer": {"servers": [{"url": "http://api:19980"}]}}},
            "middlewares": {"m1": {"headers": {}}},
        }
    }
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        traefik_tools.traefik_manager, "build_config", lambda: config
    )

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="config").user_response

    assert "1 router(s), 1 service(s), 1 middleware(s)" in text
    assert '"r1"' in text
    assert "Host(`a.test`)" in text


def test_static_config_file_is_redacted(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    config_file = tmp_path / "traefik.yaml"
    config_file.write_text(
        "api:\n  dashboard: true\ncertificatesResolvers:\n  ssl:\n    acme:\n"
        "      storage: /config/acme.json\n      keyPassword: hunter2\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.setenv(traefik_tools.CONFIG_PATH_ENV, str(config_file))

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="config", source="file").user_response

    assert "dashboard: true" in text
    assert "hunter2" not in text
    assert "keyPassword: ***" in text


def test_logs_filter_and_count_failures(monkeypatch):
    logs = "\n".join([
        '{"level":"info","msg":"Configuration loaded"}',
        '{"ClientHost":"1.2.3.4","RouterName":"codx-junior@docker","DownstreamStatus":200}',
        '{"RouterName":"codx-junior-api@docker","DownstreamStatus":502,"msg":"error"}',
    ])
    monkeypatch.setattr(traefik_tools, "_docker", DockerStub(logs_output=logs))

    text = traefik_tools.traefik(action="logs", search="codx-junior-api").user_response

    assert "1 shown" in text
    assert "DownstreamStatus\":502" in text
    assert "Configuration loaded" not in text
    assert "1 with an error/status marker" in text


def test_logs_without_container_reports_the_env_var():
    assert True  # covered by test_status_without_container_is_actionable

    def __init__(self):

        if isinstance(target, str) and value is None:
            module_name, _, attribute = target.rpartition(".")
            target = sys.modules[module_name]
            name, value = attribute, name
        old = getattr(target, name, None)
        self._undo.append(lambda: setattr(target, name, old))

        self._undo.append(

        old = os.environ.pop(name, None)
        if old is not None:

    """

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stack detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _package_dependencies(project_path: Path) -> List[str]:
    """Read package.json dependency names (best effort)."""
    package_json = project_path / "package.json"
    if not package_json.is_file():
        return []
    try:
        data = json.loads(package_json.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    names: List[str] = []
    for section in ("dependencies", "devDependencies", "peerDependencies"):
        names.extend((data.get(section) or {}).keys())
    return names


def detect_stack(project_paths: Iterable[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Inspect project folders and return a small, human-readable stack summary.

    The scan is bounded (files, depth, ignored folders), so a huge repository
    cannot block the assistant.
    """
    extensions: Counter = Counter()
    manifests: set = set()
    packages: set = set()
    has_tests = False
    files_seen = 0
    paths = [str(path) for path in project_paths if path]

    for raw_path in paths:
        if not raw_path:
            continue
        project_path = Path(raw_path)
        if not project_path.is_dir():
            continue
        for name in MANIFESTS:
            if (project_path / name).is_file():
                manifests.add(name)
        packages.update(_package_dependencies(project_path))

        base_depth = len(project_path.parts)
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(project_path):
            dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in IGNORED_DIRS]
            depth = len(Path(root).parts) - base_depth
            if depth > MAX_SCAN_DEPTH:
                dirs[:] = []
                continue
            for filename in files:
                if files_seen >= MAX_SCAN_FILES:
                    break
                files_seen += 1
                suffix = Path(filename).suffix.lower()
                for language, suffixes in LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS.items():
                    if suffix in suffixes:
                        extensions[language] += 1
                        break
                if filename in ("Dockerfile", "docker-compose.yml", "docker-compose.yaml"):
                    manifests.add(filename)
                if filename.startswith("test_") or filename.endswith("_test.py") \
                        or ".test." in filename or ".spec." in filename:
                    has_tests = True
            if files_seen >= MAX_SCAN_FILES:
                break

    languages = [language for language, _ in extensions.most_common(5)]
    frameworks: List[str] = []
    lower_packages = {package.lower() for package in packages}
    if lower_packages & set(FRONTEND_PACKAGES) or "vue" in languages or "svelte" in languages:
        frameworks.append("frontend")
    if lower_packages & set(BACKEND_PACKAGES):
        frameworks.append("backend")
    if lower_packages & set(TEST_PACKAGES) or has_tests:
        frameworks.append("tests")
    if any("docker" in name.lower() for name in manifests):
        frameworks.append("docker")
    if "pyproject.toml" in manifests or "requirements.txt" in manifests:
        frameworks.append("python")
    if "package.json" in manifests:
        frameworks.append("node")
    # CI/config heuristics (cheap checks on the first project root).
    for raw_path in paths:
        if not raw_path:
            continue
        root = Path(raw_path)
        if (root / ".github" / "workflows").is_dir():
            frameworks.append("ci")
        if (root / "terraform.tf").is_file() or (root / "infra").is_dir():
            frameworks.append("infra")
        break

    parts: List[str] = []
    if languages:
        parts.append("Languages: " + ", ".join(languages))
    if frameworks:
        parts.append("Detected: " + ", ".join(sorted(set(frameworks))))
    if manifests:
        parts.append("Manifests: " + ", ".join(sorted(manifests)[:8]))
    return {
        "languages": languages,
        "frameworks": sorted(set(frameworks)),
        "manifests": sorted(manifests),
        "has_tests": has_tests or "tests" in frameworks,
        "has_docker": "docker" in frameworks,
        "files_seen": files_seen,
        "summary": " · ".join(parts) or "No obvious stack detected",
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recommendation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _match_preset(need: str) -> Optional[str]:
    lowered = (need or "").lower()
    for preset_id, preset in TEAM_PRESETS.items():
        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in preset["keywords"]):
            return preset_id
    return None


def _match_roles(need: str) -> List[str]:
    lowered = (need or "").lower()
    roles: List[str] = []
    for role_id, role in ROLES.items():
        if role_id == "it_lead":
            continue
        if any(keyword in lowered for keyword in role["keywords"]):
            roles.append(role_id)
    # A specialized developer role replaces the generic one for the same need.
    if any(role in roles for role in ("frontend_developer", "backend_developer")):
        roles = [role for role in roles if role != "developer"]
    # A manager/lead request maps to the IT lead when no other role matched.
    if not roles and any(word in lowered for word in ("manager", "lead", "head of")):
        roles.append("it_lead")
    # "developer" is the safe default for a generic "I need someone to build X".
    if not roles:
        roles.append("developer")
    return list(dict.fromkeys(roles))


def _clean_profile_name(value: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "_", value or "").strip("._") or "profile"


def _team_name_for(need: str, mode: str, roles: List[str]) -> str:
    preset_id = _match_preset(need)
    if preset_id:
        return TEAM_PRESETS[preset_id]["team_name"]
    if mode == "team":
        if "developer" in roles and "qa_engineer" in roles:
            return "Engineering Team"
        if "data_analyst" in roles:
            return "Data Team"
        if "designer" in roles:
            return "Design Team"
        if "support_engineer" in roles:
            return "Support Team"
        return "Company Team"
    title = ROLES[roles[0]]["title"]
    return f"{title} Team"


def recommend(
    need: str,
    *,
    company_name: str = "",
    available_profiles: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
    available_tools: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None,
    projects: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Recommend profiles and a team for a plain-language need.

    Args:
        need: What the manager asked for ("I need an IT team", …).
        company_name: Company name, used in generated instructions.
        available_profiles: Profile names visible from the target project.
        available_tools: Tool names registered in the runtime.
        projects: Discovered projects with ``project_id``, ``project_name`` and
            ``project_path``.

    Returns:
        A serializable suggestion: ``mode`` (profile/team), ``team_name``,
        ``project``, ``stack``, ``roles`` and a markdown ``summary``.
    """
    profiles = [str(name) for name in (available_profiles or [])]
    tools = set(str(name) for name in (available_tools or []))
    project_list = list(projects or [])
    project = project_list[0] if project_list else {}

    preset_id = _match_preset(need)
    if preset_id:
        preset = TEAM_PRESETS[preset_id]
        role_ids = list(preset["roles"])
        mode = "team"
    else:
        role_ids = _match_roles(need)
        mode = "team" if len(role_ids) > 1 or " team" in f" {need} ".lower() else "profile"

    stack = detect_stack(
        [project.get("project_path") for project in project_list if project.get("project_path")]
    )

    roles: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    for role_id in role_ids:
        role = ROLES[role_id]
        existing = [name for name in profiles if name == role["profile_name"]]
        bases = [name for name in role["bases"] if name in profiles]
        fallback = next(
            (name for name in ("software_developer", "analyst", "project", "orchestrator") if name in profiles),
            profiles[0] if profiles else "",
        )
        if not bases and fallback:
            bases = [fallback]
        # A project profile can always be created; a base profile is preferred
        # but not mandatory (the generated instructions still work).
        create = not existing and bool(project.get("project_id"))
        profile_name = role["profile_name"] if create or existing else (
            bases[0] if bases else role["profile_name"]
        )
        selected_tools = list(dict.fromkeys(
            tool for tool in role["tools"] if not tools or tool in tools
        ))
        roles.append({
            "role_id": role_id,
            "title": role["title"],
            "profile_name": profile_name,
            "description": role["description"],
            "category": role["category"],
            "bases": bases,
            "tools": selected_tools,
            "responsibilities": list(role["responsibilities"]),
            "create": create,
            "existing": bool(existing),
            "reason": _role_reason(role_id, stack, need),
        })

    team_name = _team_name_for(need, mode, role_ids)
    summary = _summary(need, company_name, project, stack, roles, mode, team_name)
    return {
        "need": need.strip(),
        "mode": mode,
        "team_name": team_name,
        "project_id": project.get("project_id", ""),
        "project_name": project.get("project_name", ""),
        "stack": stack,
        "roles": roles,
        "summary": summary,
    }


def _role_reason(role_id: str, stack: Dict[str, Any], need: str) -> str:
    languages = ", ".join(stack.get("languages") or []) or "the detected project"
    reason = {
        "it_lead": "someone has to turn your requests into work for the team",
        "developer": f"the project uses {languages} and needs someone to change the code",
        "frontend_developer": "the project has a user interface that must be built and checked",
        "backend_developer": "the project exposes services/data that must stay reliable",
        "qa_engineer": "changes must be tested before you accept them",
        "devops_engineer": "the project needs someone to run containers/deployments"
        if stack.get("has_docker") else "the project needs someone to keep it running",
        "security_engineer": "someone should review changes for security and privacy",
        "data_analyst": "the project needs its numbers turned into decisions",
        "designer": "the product needs a consistent visual and content direction",
        "product_manager": "someone must keep the work aligned with the company goal",
        "technical_writer": "the team and customers need clear documentation",
        "support_engineer": "users need someone to reproduce and solve their problems",
    }
    return reason.get(role_id, "this role matches what you asked for")


def _summary(
    need: str,
    company_name: str,
    project: Dict[str, Any],
    stack: Dict[str, Any],
    roles: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    mode: str,
    team_name: str,
) -> str:
    project_name = project.get("project_name") or "the project"
    lines = [
        f"### For “{need.strip()}”",
        f"I looked at **{project_name}** — {stack.get('summary', 'no stack detected')}.",
        "",
    ]
    if mode == "team":
        lines.append(f"I'd create **{team_name}** with:")
    else:
        lines.append("I'd set up this profile:")
    for role in roles:
        action = "reuse" if role["existing"] else ("create" if role["create"] else "use")
        bases = ", ".join(role["bases"]) or "no base profile"
        lines.append(
            f"- **{role['title']}** — {action} `{role['profile_name']}` "
            f"(based on: {bases})"
        )
        lines.append(f"  {role['reason']}.")
    if stack.get("has_docker"):
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("The project uses Docker, so the team also gets container tools.")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def profile_content(
    role: Dict[str, Any],
    *,
    company_name: str,
    project_name: str,
    stack: Dict[str, Any],
) -> str:
    """Generate the Markdown instructions of a new profile."""
    bases = ", ".join(role.get("bases") or []) or "none"
    tools = ", ".join(role.get("tools") or []) or "the tools granted by the project"
    responsibilities = "\n".join(
        f"- {item}" for item in role.get("responsibilities") or []
    )
    stack_summary = stack.get("summary") or "No stack detected"
    return f"""# {role.get('title', role.get('profile_name'))}

You are the **{role.get('title')}** of **{company_name or 'the company'}**, working on **{project_name or 'the project'}**.

## Why you exist
{role.get('description', '')}

## What you own
{responsibilities}

## How you work
- Read the existing code and documentation before changing anything.
- Prefer small, verifiable steps over large rewrites.
- Explain decisions and risks in plain language for a non-technical manager.
- Ask for missing information instead of inventing it.
- Leave the project in a better state than you found it.

## Project context
- Stack: {stack_summary}
- Base profiles: {bases}
- Tools available: {tools}

## Handover
When you finish, summarize what changed, how it was verified and what (if
anything) the manager should decide next.
"""


# Made with ❤️ by codx-junior

# ROLE & OBJECTIVE
You are an expert AI DevOps engineer assistant. Your primary goal is to keep the running platform healthy: containers, routing, deployments and the proxy layer. You must follow a strict, structured workflow optimized for human review and incremental implementation.

# CORE DIRECTIVES
1. **Tool-First Discovery**: Always use available tools to explore the filesystem, locate existing files, and understand project architecture before writing code or requesting information.
2. **Delay Implementation**: Do not rush to modify files. Fully comprehend the issue, trace execution paths, and understand all dependencies before generating code.
3. **New File Constraint**: Create new files *only* when exhaustive search confirms the required functionality does not exist in the current codebase. Reuse or extend existing modules whenever possible.
4. **Minimal Changes**: Focus exclusively on the specific problem. Avoid refactoring, formatting cleanup, or architectural changes unless explicitly requested.
5. **Evidence Before Action**: Never restart, rebuild or recreate a service before showing the state that justifies it (logs, inspect, route table).

# TRAEFIK & ROUTING (READ THIS BEFORE DEBUGGING ANY URL)
codx-junior publishes almost every URL through Traefik: the SPA, the API
(`/api`), the auth middleware (`codx-junior-auth`), workspace apps, LocalAI, the
Traefik dashboard (`/traefik`) and every custom route. The routing table is
**generated by codx-junior** and polled by Traefik from
`GET /api/traefik/config` every 10 seconds.

Use the `traefik` tool first for anything that looks like a routing problem
("404", "502", "bad gateway", "the app is not reachable", "my route disappeared"):

| `traefik(action=…)` | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | Is the container running? Restarts? Effective command line, HTTP provider endpoint, static-config location and route statistics with open issues. |
| `routes` | The merged routing table (workspace / global / project) with rule, target, `managed_by`, enabled flag and per-route issues. Filter with `search`. |
| `config` (`source="file"`) | The static `traefik.yaml` (entrypoints, providers, ACME, access log settings); `source="generated"` returns the dynamic config Traefik actually polls. |
| `logs` | Container logs, **access logs included** (JSON), filterable with `search`; credentials in headers are masked automatically. |

Diagnostic order that resolves most incidents:

1. `traefik(action="status")` — a restart loop or a missing provider explains the symptom before any code reading.
2. `traefik(action="routes", search="<path or host>")` — if the route is missing or `enabled: no`, the problem is in the rule (config), not in the proxy.
3. `traefik(action="logs", search="<router or path>", tail=50)` — a `502` with `RouterName` set means Traefik matched the route but could not reach the backend; then use `docker_ps` / `docker_logs` on that backend.
4. `traefik(action="config", source="file")` — only when the provider itself is in question.

Rules of thumb:
* The HTTP provider endpoint **must** use the internal service name (`http://codx-junior-api:19980/api/traefik/config`); the public domain does not expose that port.
* Container routes are defined by Docker labels; codx-junior only *displays* them. Editing them means editing the container/compose labels, not the UI.
* HTTP-provider routes reference the auth middleware as `codx-junior-auth@docker` (override with `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_AUTH_MIDDLEWARE`).
* `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_CONTAINER` / `CODX_JUNIOR_TRAEFIK_CONFIG` point the tool at a different container name or static config path when the deployment differs from the installer.

# WORKFLOW & OUTPUT STRUCTURE
Your response must strictly follow this 4-part structure:

## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking
- **Core Requirements**: [Briefly state main objectives]
- **Observed State**: [What the tools reported: container status, route rows, log lines]
- **Strategic Approach**: [Step-by-step logic]
- **Dependencies & Risks**: [Edge cases, side effects, impacts]
- **Target Files**: [List files to be created/modified/deleted]

## 2. Minimum Changes Approach
Process files sequentially. One section per file. Allow user validation before proceeding. Focus only on changes made.

## 3. File changes, Code Block Formatting & Proposed Changes
- Generate this section only for files with changes.
- Use exact language identifier + full absolute/relative path: ` ```language /path/to/file.ext `
- Provide **full file content** with all changes applied.
- Match original formatting/indentation exactly.
- One code block per file.

```txt code_block/example.txt
This is an example on how to create a codse block.
Add always the file path after the extension or code block language.
```

## 4. File Change Summary Tables
Immediately follow each code block with a Markdown table:
| File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `/path/to/file` | Modify/Create | `function_name` | [Specific change description] |

# HANDLING MISSING INFORMATION
- **Proactively request** missing files, code snippets, or clarifications before implementation.
- **Never invent, assume, or hallucinate** code, paths, or functionality.
- Use this format if context is missing:

# Workspaces

Workspaces are dev containers managed by codx-junior. They run your projects with Docker Compose and publish their apps through Traefik, so the whole team works from the browser.

![Desktop](/images/NOV2025/codx-junior-desktop.png)

## Templates

| Template | What it creates |
| --- | --- |
| `dev-stack` | A `devbox` container running with Sysbox: systemd and its own Docker daemon, without `--privileged` or the host Docker socket. Good for full stack development. |
| `static-site` | An `app` container (default image `node:22-slim`) that runs `npm install && npm run dev`. The image and command can be changed with the `IMAGE` and `COMMAND` variables. |
| `custom` | Your own `docker-compose.yaml`. codx-junior can generate the files with AI from a description. |

## Settings

* **Projects** mounted into the workspace.
* **Users** allowed to use it (empty means everyone).
* **Apps**: name, icon, path, port and scheme. Each app is published under a path on your domain and protected by codx-junior's login.
* **Environment variables** and **resources** (CPUs, memory, shared memory).
* **Sysbox** on or off.

The workspace files (compose file, Dockerfile, env) can be edited from the UI. You can start, stop and restart workspaces, follow their status (`stopped`, `starting`, `running`, `error`) and read their logs.

## Custom Traefik rules

Besides the Traefik labels generated for workspace apps, admins can define custom routes from **Settings → Global settings → Traefik** and **Settings → Project settings → Traefik**. Both screens use the same editor, but they write to different stores:

| Scope | Stored in | Travels with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global | `GlobalSettings.traefik_rules` | the codx-junior installation |
| Project | `.codx/project.json` (`CODXJuniorSettings.traefik_rules`) | the project, so it keeps its routes in another codx-junior instance |

The merged list shows three kinds of routes:

* **Workspace**: generated from the workspace apps. Container apps are still routed by their Docker labels; external-URL apps are published by the HTTP provider.
* **Global**: custom rules available to every project.
* **Project**: custom rules owned by one project.

A custom rule can target:

* a **workspace app** (it reuses the label-defined Traefik service, or the external URL service);
* a **running container** (`http://<container-name>:<port>`, with Traefik and the container sharing a Docker network);
* an **external URL**.

Each rule has a full Traefik rule expression (for example ``Host(`app.example.com`) && PathPrefix(`/app`)``), an optional strip-prefix middleware, the auth middleware, extra middlewares, entrypoints and a priority. Every enabled rule is published through `GET /api/traefik/config`, which Traefik polls every 10 seconds.

Project scope is organizational: Traefik is a single proxy, so every enabled global and project rule is published together. The project scope decides where the rule is stored and edited, not whether it is active.

http://codx-junior-api:19980/api/traefik/config

"""
Tab (page) management for the shared browser session.

The browser container is a real Chromium window: the user watches it through the
live VNC view while the AI drives it over CDP, so tabs are a **shared** resource.
Opening, selecting and closing them must be visible in that same window.

``Browser`` (``codx.junior.browser.browser``) owns the connection and the page
automation primitives; this module adds the tab primitives it deliberately does
not cover, operating on a connected ``Browser``:

    tabs = await list_tabs(browser)         # every tab + active flag
    tab  = await open_tab(browser, url)     # new tab, navigated and focused
    tab  = await switch_tab(browser, index) # move the AI (and the user) to it
    tab  = await close_tab(browser, index)  # close one, activate the next

Keep-alive tab
--------------
Chromium exits when its **last window closes**, and the container keeps running
(the desktop session is still alive), so the live view stays up while the
browser window is gone: neither the user nor the AI can reach the page again
until the browser process is restarted.

To make that impossible by accident, every session owns one **keep-alive tab**
(``about:blank#codx-keep-alive``, titled "codx-junior · keep this tab open"):

- ``ensure_keep_alive_tab`` creates it once and reactivates the working tab, so
  closing every other tab leaves the window (and Chromium) alive;
- ``close_tab`` refuses to close it;
- ``ensure_page`` reopens a page when, despite the guard, the browser ends up
  with no tabs at all (see ``BrowserManager.connect_browser`` for the full
  recovery of a dead browser).

Conventions
-----------
- the *tab index* is the position of the page in ``context.pages`` (stable while
  no tab is opened or closed); that is what the agent tools expose;
- ``browser.page`` always points at the tab the AI drives;
- every selection is brought to front, so the live view shows the tab the AI is
  working on (co-browsing);
- the keep-alive tab and the last tab are never closed: closing them would close
  the browser window the user is watching.
"""

import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Hard cap on the tabs an agent may open (they are all visible to the user).
MAX_TABS = 20

#: Fragment identifying the protected tab (survives reconnections).
KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT = "codx-keep-alive"
#: URL of the protected tab (``about:blank`` + marker fragment).
KEEP_ALIVE_URL = f"about:blank#{KEEP_ALIVE_FRAGMENT}"
#: Title of the protected tab (what the user reads in the tab strip).
KEEP_ALIVE_TITLE = "codx-junior · keep this tab open"
#: Content of the protected tab: explains

```py api/codx/junior/browser/cdp_proxy.py
Playwright connects to ``ws://…/devtools/browser/<id>`` and that id changes every
time Chromium restarts, so a cached WebSocket URL becomes stale (404) and the
caller has to fall back to restarting the whole container.  The proxy rewrites
the ``/devtools/browser/<id>`` path of the incoming handshake to the id the
browser currently reports, keeping the endpoint stable across browser restarts.
Best effort: when the current id cannot be read the path is left untouched.

Environment variables:
    CDP_PROXY_LISTEN_HOST  Host/interface to listen on (default ``0.0.0.0``).
    CDP_PROXY_LISTEN_PORT  Exposed proxy port (default ``9223``).
    CDP_TARGET_HOST        DevTools host (default ``127.0.0.1``).
    CDP_TARGET_PORT        DevTools port (default ``9222``).
    CDP_REWRITE_HOST       Value written in the ``Host`` header (default
                           ``127.0.0.1:9222``).
    CDP_GUARD              Keep the browser alive (default ``1``; ``0`` disables).
    CDP_GUARD_INTERVAL     Seconds between checks (default ``2``).
    CDP_GUARD_GRACE        Seconds to wait after start before acting (default ``30``).
    CDP_GUARD_DEAD_THRESHOLD  Unreachable checks before restarting (default ``3``).
    CDP_GUARD_COOLDOWN     Minimum seconds between two browser restarts (default ``15``).
    CDP_GUARD_HTTP_TIMEOUT Timeout of the local DevTools requests (default ``3``).
    CDP_STABLE_BROWSER_ID  Rewrite the browser id (default ``1``; ``0`` disables).
"""

import asyncio
import contextlib
import functools
import json
import logging
import os
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional
from urllib.parse import urlparse

LISTEN_HOST = os.environ.get("CDP_PROXY_LISTEN_HOST", "0.0.0.0")
LISTEN_PORT = int(os.environ.get("CDP_PROXY_LISTEN_PORT", "9223"))
TARGET_HOST = os.environ.get("CDP_TARGET_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
TARGET_PORT = int(os.environ.get("CDP_TARGET_PORT", "9222"))
REWRITE_HOST = os.environ.get("CDP_REWRITE_HOST", f"{TARGET_HOST}:{TARGET_PORT}")
CHUNK_SIZE = 64 * 1024

                print("   ", pg)
            await b.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Throwaway probe: does connecting over CDP add tabs? (delete after use)"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import urllib.request

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright


def ws_url(http_base):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{http_base}/json/version", timeout=10) as resp:
        version = json.load(resp)
    raw = version["webSocketDebuggerUrl"]  # ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser/<id>
    path = raw.split("9222", 1)[-1]
    return f"{http_base.replace('http://', 'ws://')}{path if path.startswith('/') else '/' + path}"


async def main(http_base):
    cdp = ws_url(http_base)
    print("cdp:", cdp)
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        for i in range(3):
            browser = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp)
            context = browser.contexts[0]
            print(f"connect #{i + 1}: {len(context.pages)} page(s)")
            for page in context.pages:
                print("   ", (page.url or "")[:60])
            await browser.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1]))

"""Throwaway probe: tab inventory of every running browser session (delete after use)."""
import asyncio
import json
import subprocess
import urllib.request

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright


def containers():
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "ps", "--format", "{{.Names}}"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30,
    ).stdout.split()
    return [name for name in out if name.startswith("browser_")]


def ws_url(name):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://{name}:9223/json/version", timeout=5) as resp:
        version = json.load(resp)
    path = version["webSocketDebuggerUrl"].split("9222", 1)[-1]
    return f"ws://{name}:9223{path if path.startswith('/') else '/' + path}"


async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        for name in containers():
            try:
                cdp = ws_url(name)
            except Exception as ex:
                print(f"{name}: unreachable ({ex})")
                continue
            try:
                browser = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(cdp)
                pages = [page.url or "" for page in browser.contexts[0].pages]
                await browser.close()
            except Exception as ex:
                print(f"{name}: connect failed ({ex})")
                continue

def devtools_status(host: Optional[str] = None, port: Optional[int] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Probe the local browser: is DevTools alive and does it have any tab?

    Args:
        host: DevTools host (defaults to :data:`TARGET_HOST`).
        port: DevTools port (defaults to :data:`TARGET_PORT`).

    Returns:
        Dict[str, Any]: ``alive`` (DevTools answers), ``pages`` (number of page
        targets) and ``error`` when something failed.

    Example:
        >>> devtools_status()["alive"]
        True
    """
    base = f"http://{host or TARGET_HOST}:{port or TARGET_PORT}"

    try:
        _http_json(f"{base}/json/version")
    except Exception as ex:
        return {"alive": False, "pages": 0, "error": str(ex)}

    try:
        targets = _http_json(f"{base}/json/list")
    except Exception as ex:
        # The version endpoint answered but the target list did not: the browser
        # is up but not usable yet (still starting). Never treated as dead.
        return {"alive": True, "pages": 0, "error": str(ex)}

    pages = [
        target for target in (targets or [])
        if str(target.get("type") or "") == "page" and not target.get("closed")
    ]
    return {
        "alive": True,
        "pages": len(pages),
        "urls": [page.get("url") for page in pages][:5],
    }


def open_tab(url: str = "about:blank", host: Optional[str] = None, port: Optional[int] = None) -> bool:
    """
    Open a tab in the running browser (brings the window back when it had none).

    Recent Chromium only accepts ``PUT`` on ``/json/new``; older builds accept
    ``GET``, so both are tried.

    Args:
        url: URL opened in the new tab.
        host: DevTools host (defaults to :data:`TARGET_HOST`).
        port: DevTools port (defaults to :data:`TARGET_PORT`).

    Returns:
        bool: True when the tab could be created.

    Example:
        >>> open_tab()  # doctest: +SKIP
        True
    """
    target = f"http://{host or TARGET_HOST}:{port or TARGET_PORT}/json/new?{url}"
    for method in ("PUT", "GET"):
        try:
            _http_json(target, method=method, payload=b"" if method == "PUT" else None)
            return True
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Could not open a tab with %s: %s", method, ex)
    return False

/**
 * User-facing labels of the co-desktop concept.
 *
 * The concept used to be called "computer sessions" and, for a while, "Machines".
 * It is now called **"Co-desktops"**: a desktop (real machine, VM or browser)
 * that the user and the AI share. The section/navigation entry is `section`
 * ("Co-desktops"), one entry is `item` ("Co-desktop"), and `live` ("Live
 * session") is reserved for the running / handoff state of a co-desktop the user
 * has to look at.
 *
 * EVERY user-facing string that names the concept must come from this module so
 * that a future rename is one edit here instead of a tree-wide search and
 * replace. It holds display strings only: never use these values as ids, route
 * names, API/model fields, store keys or i18n keys — those keep their current
 * names on purpose (backwards compatibility).
 *
 * Placeholders in `{name}` form are filled in by `label(key, vars)`.
 */

export const SESSION_LABELS = Object.freeze({
  // ── Section / navigation ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  section: 'Co-desktops',
  sectionHint: 'Your co-desktops and their live screens',

  // ── One item of the section ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  item: 'Co-desktop',
  items: 'Co-desktops',
  itemShort: 'Co-desktop',
  untitled: 'Co-desktop',
  newItem: 'New co-desktop',
  create: 'New co-desktop',
  createError: 'Could not create the co-desktop',

  // ── Running / handoff state (never the section name) ────────────────────
  live: 'Live session',
  needsYou: 'Needs you',
  needsYouHint: 'This co-desktop is waiting for you',
  running: 'Running',
  stopped: 'Stopped',

  // ── List states ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  loading: 'Loading co-desktops…',
  empty: 'No co-desktops yet',
  emptyHint: 'Create a co-desktop to get a desktop with the project files inside',
  loadError: 'Could not load co-desktops',
  loadErrorHint: 'The list of co-desktops could not be fetched',
  retry: 'Retry loading co-desktops',
  retryShort: 'Retry',
  reload: 'Reload co-desktops',
  noSelection: 'Select a co-desktop',

  // ── Actions (use the {name} placeholder) ────────────────────────────────
  selectItem: 'Select co-desktop {name}',
  runItem: 'Run co-desktop {name}',
  editItem: 'Edit co-desktop {name}',
  deleteItem: 'Delete co-desktop {name}',
  deleteTitle: 'Delete co-desktop',
  deleteConfirm: "Delete co-desktop '{name}'?",
  deleteHint: 'The session, its profile and its desktop state will be removed. This cannot be undone.',

  // ── Views ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  singleHint: 'Single view: one co-desktop',
  singleHintLong: 'One co-desktop at a time',
  gridHint: 'Grid view: several co-desktops at once',
  gridHintLong: 'Watch several co-desktops at once',
  wallTitle: 'Co-desktops on the wall',
  wallPick: 'Select the co-desktops on the wall',
  wallPickHint: 'Choose the co-desktops on the wall',
  wallPickShort: 'Co-desktops',
  gridPick: 'Pick the co-desktops you want to watch at the same time',
  gridEmpty: 'No co-desktops on the wall',
  gridWall: 'Wall of co-desktops',

  // ── Image library of the concept ────────────────────────────────────────
  imageLibrary: 'Co-desktop image library',
  browseImages: 'Browse the co-desktop image library'
})

/**
 * Reads a label by key and fills its `{name}` placeholders.
 *
 * Falls back to the key itself so a typo or a not-yet-migrated caller never
 * renders `undefined` in the UI.
 *
 * @param {string} key key of {@link SESSION_LABELS}
 * @param {Record<string, string|number>} [vars] values for the placeholders
 * @returns {string}
 */
export function label(key, vars) {
  const text = SESSION_LABELS[key] ?? key
  if (!vars) return text
  return String(text).replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (match, name) => (
    vars[name] === undefined || vars[name] === null ? match : String(vars[name])
  ))
}

export default SESSION_LABELS
