```md docs/features/computer-use.md
# Computer use: AI-assisted desktops, VMs and remote machines

Computer sessions generalize browser sessions. A session is **one real machine
shared by the user and the AI**: the human watches and can take over through a
live view, the AI drives the same screen through desktop tools. The original
Chromium sessions are now the `browser` kind of this model, so nothing is lost.
| Kind | What runs | AI control | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `browser` | Chromium container | Chrome DevTools Protocol | The existing browser co-pilot (DOM snapshots, scripts, downloads). |
| `linux` | LinuxServer.io webtop desktop container (Xvfb + KDE/XFCE + Selkies) | `docker exec` with `xdotool` + Pillow screenshots | A full Linux desktop: terminals, IDEs, GUI apps, package installs. |
| `windows` | `dockurr/windows` QEMU VM | VNC (RFB) | Windows-only software, testing an installer, Windows browsers. |
| `macos` | `dockurr/macos` QEMU VM or a remote Mac | VNC (RFB) + optional SSH | Xcode/Simulator, macOS-only tooling; a physical Mac via Screen Sharing. |
| `remote` | An existing machine reachable over VNC | VNC (RFB) + optional SSH | A Mac mini in the office, a lab workstation, a cloud desktop. |

## Why this design

Browser automation answers "what is in the DOM"; a computer needs "what is on
the screen and how do I click it". The implementation follows the same pattern
that projects such as [OpenHands](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/architecture/runtime)
and Anthropic's [computer-use demo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/tree/main/computer-use-demo)
use: a containerized desktop, a live VNC view for the human, and an
input/screenshot channel for the agent. Instead of requiring one agent binary
inside every image:

- **Linux** uses the image's own X11 tools. A small script
  (`computer/agent/computer_agent.py`) is mounted read-only and executed through
  `docker exec`; no extra port or daemon is exposed. Screenshots come from
  Pillow's X11 grab, input from `xdotool`.
- **Windows/macOS/remote** use a pure-Python RFB client
  (`computer/vnc.py`). QEMU exposes a standard VNC server on port 5900, so the
  same code works for the dockurr VMs and for a real Mac with Screen Sharing.
  The human gets the same framebuffer through a noVNC client in the panel.
- **OCR everywhere.** `computer/ocr.py` runs tesseract on every screenshot and
  returns word boxes. The model reads terminal output, dialog labels and menus,
  and `click_text` clicks the centre of a matched word, so it does not have to
  guess pixel coordinates or have vision.

Reference projects worth reading: [trycua/cua](https://github.com/trycua/cua)
(computer-use sandboxes for macOS/Linux/Windows), [dockur/windows](https://github.com/dockur/windows)
and [dockur/macos](https://github.com/dockur/macos) (OS in Docker),
[LinuxServer.io webtop/Selkies](https://docs.linuxserver.io/selkies/components/selkies/),
and [noVNC](https://github.com/novnc/noVNC).

## Image library (Kasmweb + LinuxServer.io)

The **Library** button in the Co-desktops sidebar opens the standalone
image browser (`ComputerImageLibrary.vue`): search, category chips, provider
tabs and image details.  Picking an image opens the new-session dialog with that
image already selected.  The same browser is also embedded in the new-session
dialog under **Desktop image**.  The library ships with two curated providers
and resolves the live-view transport automatically:

| Provider | Examples | Live view | AI control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **LinuxServer.io** | `webtop:debian-kde`, `ubuntu-xfce`, `ubuntu-kde`, `fedora-xfce`, `arch-i3`, `latest` (Alpine XFCE) | Selkies on `3000` (HTTP, path prefix) | `docker exec` agent (`xdotool`/Pillow) |
| **Kasmweb** | `desktop`, `ubuntu-jammy-desktop`, `core-kali-rolling`, `alma/rocky/oracle` desktops, `firefox`, `chrome`, `vs-code`, `terminal`, `libre-office`, `gimp`, … | KasmVNC on `6901` (HTTPS, stripped prefix) | `docker exec` agent (libX11/XTest + `xwd` fallback) |

The selector shows name, category, description, screenshot/logo, provider and
default tag.  Selecting a Kasmweb card loads its Docker Hub tags so a specific
release can be pinned; LinuxServer flavours are themselves the image tags and
therefore already appear as cards.  Any other `registry/image:tag` can be
entered under **Custom image**; unknown images use the screenshot fallback until
a known profile is chosen.

Kasmweb images are started with `VNC_PW`, `VNC_RESOLUTION`, `--shm-size=512m`
and the API user's group so shared project folders stay writable.  KasmVNC uses
a self-signed HTTPS certificate; Traefik reaches it through a shared
`codx-insecure` transport, injects the per-session Basic auth for the iframe,
and strips `/computer/<id>` so KasmVNC's relative assets/websocket work.  The
per-session KasmVNC login is also available from the viewer banner (and from
`POST /api/computers/{id}/viewer-credentials`).

LinuxServer images keep the existing `/config` profile persistence.  Kasmweb's
home directory is container-local (project files and downloads are shared), so
desktop preferences reset when the container is recreated.

## Saved computers (reuse a customized desktop)

The floppy-disk button in a running Linux/Kasmweb desktop commits the container
to a local Docker image and adds a **Saved** entry to the project's image
library. The AI can do the same with the `save_computer` tool when asked. The creation
dialog's image selector has a **Saved** tab; selecting an entry starts a new
session from that snapshot.

What is stored in `.codx/computer_library/<item-id>/`:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `item.json` | image, provider, live-view profile, author, size, defaults |
| `preview.png` | screenshot captured at save time |
| `profile.tar.gz` | optional LinuxServer `/config` archive (caches excluded) |

The committed image contains installed packages and changes in the container
filesystem.  LinuxServer's `/config` is a bind mount, so its settings are only
included when **Include home/profile data** is ticked; profiles may contain
logins, cookies and keys.  Kasmweb's home lives inside the container and is
always part of the commit, so the save dialog warns that it is shared with
project users.

Saved entries keep the source provider/live-view settings (`Selkies` on 3000
or `KasmVNC` on 6901) and resource/env defaults.  Starting from a saved entry
restores the optional profile before the container starts; image names like
`codx-saved/<project>/<name>:<timestamp>` are never re-canonicalised to their
upstream base.

Saving is limited to Linux desktop containers.  Windows/macOS VM state lives on
the `/storage` disk volume, not in the container layer; a VM disk snapshot flow
is still needed.  Images are local to the Docker host, so they are reusable by
users of the same project on that host; a multi-host deployment needs a registry
push.  Deleting a saved entry removes its library folder and local image, but is
blocked while a session started from it is still present.

## Architecture

```text
                        codx-junior_default Docker network
 ┌────────────────────┐   docker exec (Linux)   ┌──────────────────────────┐
 │ API / agent        │ ──────────────────────► │ Linux webtop container   │
 │ DesktopRuntime     │   xdotool + Pillow      │ Xvfb + KDE + Selkies     │
 │  ├ Linux backend   │                         └──────────┬───────────────┘
 │  ├ VNC backend     │   RFB (TCP 5900)        ┌──────────▼───────────────┐
 │  └ OCR (tesseract) │ ──────────────────────► │ Windows/macOS QEMU VM    │
 └─────────┬──────────┘                         │ VNC + noVNC              │
           │ REST / WebSocket                   └──────────────────────────┘
 ┌─────────▼──────────┐   /computer/<id>/  (Linux, Selkies)
 │ User browser       │   /api/computers/<id>/vnc (Windows/macOS/remote,
 │ live view + bar    │    one-time ticket → raw RFB WebSocket bridge)
 └────────────────────┘
```

- **Session record** — one `BrowserSession`/`ComputerSession` model stores
  `kind`, `control` (`cdp`, `docker`, `vnc`), VNC/SSH endpoints, capabilities,
  desktop size, folder sharing and the control lease. Browser sessions are
  unchanged at the storage level (`.codx/browser_sessions/`), so existing
  sessions load as `kind="browser"`.
- **Containers** — `DockerBrowserManager`/`DockerComputerManager` builds a
  different `docker run` per kind:
  - browser: Chromium + CDP proxy + `/browser/<id>/` Traefik route;
  - Linux: webtop + agent mount + `/computer/<id>/` Traefik route;
  - VM: dockurr image, `/dev/kvm`, `/dev/net/tun`, `NET_ADMIN`, `/storage`
    disk, one `/shared` folder, VNC 5900 (AI + optional external client) and
    8006 (noVNC, not required by the panel).
- **Runtime** — `DesktopRuntime` owns one backend per session and a lock, so the
  AI and the human never interleave half-finished clicks or drags. It enforces
  the same control lease as the browser runtime and writes every action to the
  shared `activity.jsonl`.
- **Live view** — Linux uses the webtop Selkies iframe. Windows/macOS/remote use
  the built-in noVNC viewer: `POST /api/computers/{id}/vnc-ticket` issues a
  single-use ticket bound to that session's VNC endpoint, and the WebSocket
  bridge tunnels raw RFB bytes. The panel therefore works through the same
  origin/Traefik route without exposing the VNC port publicly.

## Using it

### From the UI

**Co-desktops** → **New co-desktop** → choose the machine:

- **Linux desktop** (default): shell, GUI apps and project folders under
  `/home/<project_name>`; downloads/saved files land in the project.
- **Windows VM** / **macOS VM**: pick the OS release. The project root is shared
  as `Z:\` (Windows) or `/shared` (macOS). **Windows/macOS VMs require KVM** on
  the Docker host.
- **Remote machine**: VNC host/port/password, plus optional SSH host/user/key
  (or password with `sshpass`) so the AI can run builds/tests.
- **Browser only**: the original Chromium co-browsing session.

The panel shows the live view plus an action bar: type text, key buttons and
shortcuts, a shell command box (when the machine has a shell), screenshot/OCR,
"Ask AI", control handoff. Clicking the screenshot in fallback mode clicks the
desktop at the corresponding display coordinate.

### From a chat

The `computer` profile provides:

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `start_computer` | Create/resume a `linux`, `windows`, `macos`, `remote` or `browser` session. Returns `session_id` and the live view. |
| `computer_action` | `screenshot`, `ocr`, `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `click_text`, `move`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `hotkey`, `wait`, `windows`, `active_window`, `focus_window`, `close_window`, `open_app`, `list_apps`, `run_command`, `screen_size`, `batch`. |
| `computer_screenshot` | Capture the screen and return OCR text + clickable word centres. |
| `computer_status` | Kind, status, control lease, desktop size, VNC/SSH endpoints. Without an id: list sessions. |
| `computer_control` | `status`, `handoff`, `take_control`, `give_back`, `pause`. |
| `computer_activity` | Recent user/AI actions (what the human did in the live view). |
| `finish_computer` | Stop (keep profile/VM storage) or delete. |

The screenshot response includes `text` and `words` (`text`, `cx`, `cy`,
`confidence`), which is how a text-only model "sees" a GUI. `click_text` matches
case-insensitively and clicks the word centre.

### Example prompts

Start a Linux desktop. Install ripgrep, clone the repo into the project folder
and run the tests; show me the desktop while it works.

# Windows
Start a Windows 11 VM and install the app from the shared folder. Tell me if
the installer needs a reboot.

# macOS / mobile development
Connect to my Mac mini over VNC (ssh user osx). Open Xcode, boot the iPhone 16
simulator, build the app and run it; use SSH for xcodebuild output.

# Remote debugging

```

### Advanced settings per session

Windows/macOS sessions show a dedicated **VM resources** section (vCPUs, RAM
and disk size) in the **New computer session** dialog. Browser/Linux sessions
keep the same resources under *Advanced settings*. The values are stored on the
session record, applied when the machine is created and preserved by restarts
that recreate the container:

| Setting | Browser / Linux | Windows / macOS VM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Docker image** | Overrides the Chromium/webtop image. A custom image must keep the same live-view and control contract. | Overrides `dockurr/windows` or `dockurr/macos`. |
| **vCPUs** | `docker run --cpus`. | `CPU_CORES` for QEMU (guest CPUs). |
| **RAM** | `docker run --memory`. | `RAM_SIZE` for QEMU (guest RAM). |
| **Disk size** | Not applicable (the container uses the host disk). | `DISK_SIZE`; used when the VM disk is first created. Increasing it and restarting the session expands the existing disk (dockurr keeps the data). |
| **Shared memory** | `docker run --shm-size` (default `2G`). | Not applicable. |
| **Desktop size** | Browser window size / Selkies manual resolution. | Resolution is controlled by the guest OS. |
| **Environment variables** | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. |

Environment names managed by codx-junior (`SUBFOLDER`, `TITLE`, `DISPLAY`,
`VERSION`, `RAM_SIZE`, `CPU_CORES`, `DISK_SIZE`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`…) are
reserved: values supplied in the advanced section cannot override them, because
breaking them would detach the live view or the AI control channel.

The same fields are editable after creation from the session's **Session
settings** screen. Use **Save & restart** to apply resource changes: Docker
cannot change CPU/RAM/disk on a running container, so the restart recreates it
while keeping the browser profile and the VM disk. For a macOS VM, 64 GB is the
upstream default; codx-junior defaults macOS to 128 GB, and 256 GB is safer when
installing Xcode/Simulator. On first boot, erase the VirtIO disk in Disk Utility
before reinstalling macOS. After expanding the disk, macOS may need the two
`diskutil` commands documented by
[dockur/macos](https://github.com/dockur/macos) to allocate the extra space.

The API needs the Docker socket (as for workspaces) and, for VMs, the host must
expose `/dev/kvm` (and `/dev/net/tun`). VMs are heavy: at least 2 GB RAM and
32 GB disk per Windows/macOS guest, plus the image pull.

## Security and limits

- **Control lease** — the AI yields while the user is driving or has taken
  control. Desktops use the same `controller`/`user_active_until`/handoff
  protocol as browsers; the AI must call `computer_control(handoff)` for
  passwords, MFA, captchas and payment approvals.
- **Secrets** — VNC/SSH passwords and the SSH key path are stripped from the
  general session record (`to_public_dict`), Socket.IO events and activity
  logs; they are stored in the session file (mode controlled by the project
  `.codx`). The VNC password is returned only by the authenticated, one-time
  `vnc-ticket` endpoint so the built-in viewer can authenticate.
- **Ticket-scoped live view** — the noVNC bridge only connects to the host/port
  captured when an authenticated HTTP request issued the ticket; tickets are
  single-use and expire in 60 s.
- **Shell** — `run_command` is powerful by design. It runs only on `linux`
  containers or on a remote session with SSH configured, is bounded by a
  timeout, and is always recorded in the activity log. The browser profile and
  the computer profile instruct the model never to exfiltrate files or secrets.
- **KVM and licensing** — Windows/macOS VMs need hardware virtualization. macOS
  in a VM is only permitted on Apple hardware per Apple's EULA; prefer
  `kind="remote"` for a real Mac.
- **Not implemented yet** — clipboard sync over VNC (use SSH or the Linux
  agent), audio, multi-monitor, and file drag-and-drop inside VMs. Windows/macOS
  guests have no shell unless SSH is configured; use the GUI terminal there.
- **Live-view input detection** — Windows/macOS/remote viewer input is reported
  by the RFB bridge, so the AI yields automatically. The Linux Selkies and
  KasmVNC iframe views do not expose input events to the API: press
  **Take control** before driving a Linux/Kasmweb desktop manually, or the AI
  may keep acting.

## Why this design

Browser automation answers "what is in the DOM"; a computer needs "what is on
the screen and how do I click it". The implementation follows the same pattern
that projects such as [OpenHands](https://docs.openhands.dev/openhands/usage/architecture/runtime)
and Anthropic's [computer-use demo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-quickstarts/tree/main/computer-use-demo)
use: a containerized desktop, a live VNC view for the human, and an
input/screenshot channel for the agent. Instead of requiring one agent binary
inside every image:

- **Linux** uses the image's own X11 tools. A small script
  (`computer/agent/computer_agent.py`) is mounted read-only and executed through
  `docker exec`; no extra port or daemon is exposed. Screenshots come from
  Pillow's X11 grab, input from `xdotool`.
- **Windows/macOS/remote** use a pure-Python RFB client
  (`computer/vnc.py`). QEMU exposes a standard VNC server on port 5900, so the
  same code works for the dockurr VMs and for a real Mac with Screen Sharing.
  The human gets the same framebuffer through a noVNC client in the panel.
- **OCR everywhere.** `computer/ocr.py` runs tesseract on every screenshot and
  returns word boxes. The model reads terminal output, dialog labels and menus,
  and `click_text` clicks the centre of a matched word, so it does not have to
  guess pixel coordinates or have vision.

Reference projects worth reading: [trycua/cua](https://github.com/trycua/cua)
(computer-use sandboxes for macOS/Linux/Windows), [dockur/windows](https://github.com/dockur/windows)
and [dockur/macos](https://github.com/dockur/macos) (OS in Docker),
[LinuxServer.io webtop/Selkies](https://docs.linuxserver.io/selkies/components/selkies/),
and [noVNC](https://github.com/novnc/noVNC).

## Image library (Kasmweb + LinuxServer.io)

The **Library** button in the Co-desktops sidebar opens the standalone
image browser (`ComputerImageLibrary.vue`): search, category chips, provider
tabs and image details.  Picking an image opens the new-session dialog with that
image already selected.  The same browser is also embedded in the new-session
dialog under **Desktop image**.  The library ships with two curated providers
and resolves the live-view transport automatically:

| Provider | Examples | Live view | AI control |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **LinuxServer.io** | `webtop:debian-kde`, `ubuntu-xfce`, `ubuntu-kde`, `fedora-xfce`, `arch-i3`, `latest` (Alpine XFCE) | Selkies on `3000` (HTTP, path prefix) | `docker exec` agent (`xdotool`/Pillow) |
| **Kasmweb** | `desktop`, `ubuntu-jammy-desktop`, `core-kali-rolling`, `alma/rocky/oracle` desktops, `firefox`, `chrome`, `vs-code`, `terminal`, `libre-office`, `gimp`, … | KasmVNC on `6901` (HTTPS, stripped prefix) | `docker exec` agent (libX11/XTest + `xwd` fallback) |

The selector shows name, category, description, screenshot/logo, provider and
default tag.  Selecting a Kasmweb card loads its Docker Hub tags so a specific
release can be pinned; LinuxServer flavours are themselves the image tags and
therefore already appear as cards.  Any other `registry/image:tag` can be
entered under **Custom image**; unknown images use the screenshot fallback until
a known profile is chosen.

Kasmweb images are started with `VNC_PW`, `VNC_RESOLUTION`, `--shm-size=512m`
and the API user's group so shared project folders stay writable.  KasmVNC uses
a self-signed HTTPS certificate; Traefik reaches it through a shared
`codx-insecure` transport, injects the per-session Basic auth for the iframe,
and strips `/computer/<id>` so KasmVNC's relative assets/websocket work.  The
per-session KasmVNC login is also available from the viewer banner (and from
`POST /api/computers/{id}/viewer-credentials`).

LinuxServer images keep the existing `/config` profile persistence.  Kasmweb's
home directory is container-local (project files and downloads are shared), so
desktop preferences reset when the container is recreated.

## Saved computers (reuse a customized desktop)

The floppy-disk button in a running Linux/Kasmweb desktop commits the container
to a local Docker image and adds a **Saved** entry to the project's image
library. The AI can do the same with the `save_computer` tool when asked. The creation
dialog's image selector has a **Saved** tab; selecting an entry starts a new
session from that snapshot.

What is stored in `.codx/computer_library/<item-id>/`:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `item.json` | image, provider, live-view profile, author, size, defaults |
| `preview.png` | screenshot captured at save time |
| `profile.tar.gz` | optional LinuxServer `/config` archive (caches excluded) |

The committed image contains installed packages and changes in the container
filesystem.  LinuxServer's `/config` is a bind mount, so its settings are only
included when **Include home/profile data** is ticked; profiles may contain
logins, cookies and keys.  Kasmweb's home lives inside the container and is
always part of the commit, so the save dialog warns that it is shared with
project users.

Saved entries keep the source provider/live-view settings (`Selkies` on 3000
or `KasmVNC` on 6901) and resource/env defaults.  Starting from a saved entry
restores the optional profile before the container starts; image names like
`codx-saved/<project>/<name>:<timestamp>` are never re-canonicalised to their
upstream base.

Saving is limited to Linux desktop containers.  Windows/macOS VM state lives on
the `/storage` disk volume, not in the container layer; a VM disk snapshot flow
is still needed.  Images are local to the Docker host, so they are reusable by
users of the same project on that host; a multi-host deployment needs a registry
push.  Deleting a saved entry removes its library folder and local image, but is
blocked while a session started from it is still present.

### Advanced settings per session

Windows/macOS sessions show a dedicated **VM resources** section (vCPUs, RAM
and disk size) in the **New computer session** dialog. Browser/Linux sessions
keep the same resources under *Advanced settings*. The values are stored on the
session record, applied when the machine is created and preserved by restarts
that recreate the container:

| Setting | Browser / Linux | Windows / macOS VM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Docker image** | Overrides the Chromium/webtop image. A custom image must keep the same live-view and control contract. | Overrides `dockurr/windows` or `dockurr/macos`. |
| **vCPUs** | `docker run --cpus`. | `CPU_CORES` for QEMU (guest CPUs). |
| **RAM** | `docker run --memory`. | `RAM_SIZE` for QEMU (guest RAM). |
| **Disk size** | Not applicable (the container uses the host disk). | `DISK_SIZE`; used when the VM disk is first created. Increasing it and restarting the session expands the existing disk (dockurr keeps the data). |
| **Shared memory** | `docker run --shm-size` (default `2G`). | Not applicable. |
| **Desktop size** | Browser window size / Selkies manual resolution. | Resolution is controlled by the guest OS. |
| **Environment variables** | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. | Extra `-e KEY=VALUE` passed to the image. |

Environment names managed by codx-junior (`SUBFOLDER`, `TITLE`, `DISPLAY`,
`VERSION`, `RAM_SIZE`, `CPU_CORES`, `DISK_SIZE`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`…) are
reserved: values supplied in the advanced section cannot override them, because
breaking them would detach the live view or the AI control channel.

The same fields are editable after creation from the session's **Session
settings** screen. Use **Save & restart** to apply resource changes: Docker
cannot change CPU/RAM/disk on a running container, so the restart recreates it
while keeping the browser profile and the VM disk. For a macOS VM, 64 GB is the
upstream default; codx-junior defaults macOS to 128 GB, and 256 GB is safer when
installing Xcode/Simulator. On first boot, erase the VirtIO disk in Disk Utility
before reinstalling macOS. After expanding the disk, macOS may need the two
`diskutil` commands documented by
[dockur/macos](https://github.com/dockur/macos) to allocate the extra space.

The API needs the Docker socket (as for workspaces) and, for VMs, the host must
expose `/dev/kvm` (and `/dev/net/tun`). VMs are heavy: at least 2 GB RAM and
32 GB disk per Windows/macOS guest, plus the image pull.

## Security and limits

- **Control lease** — the AI yields while the user is driving or has taken
  control. Desktops use the same `controller`/`user_active_until`/handoff
  protocol as browsers; the AI must call `computer_control(handoff)` for
  passwords, MFA, captchas and payment approvals.
- **Secrets** — VNC/SSH passwords and the SSH key path are stripped from the
  general session record (`to_public_dict`), Socket.IO events and activity
  logs; they are stored in the session file (mode controlled by the project
  `.codx`). The VNC password is returned only by the authenticated, one-time
  `vnc-ticket` endpoint so the built-in viewer can authenticate.
- **Ticket-scoped live view** — the noVNC bridge only connects to the host/port
  captured when an authenticated HTTP request issued the ticket; tickets are
  single-use and expire in 60 s.
- **Shell** — `run_command` is powerful by design. It runs only on `linux`
  containers or on a remote session with SSH configured, is bounded by a
  timeout, and is always recorded in the activity log. The browser profile and
  the computer profile instruct the model never to exfiltrate files or secrets.
- **KVM and licensing** — Windows/macOS VMs need hardware virtualization. macOS
  in a VM is only permitted on Apple hardware per Apple's EULA; prefer
  `kind="remote"` for a real Mac.
- **Not implemented yet** — clipboard sync over VNC (use SSH or the Linux
  agent), audio, multi-monitor, and file drag-and-drop inside VMs. Windows/macOS
  guests have no shell unless SSH is configured; use the GUI terminal there.
- **Live-view input detection** — Windows/macOS/remote viewer input is reported
  by the RFB bridge, so the AI yields automatically. The Linux Selkies and
  KasmVNC iframe views do not expose input events to the API: press
  **Take control** before driving a Linux/Kasmweb desktop manually, or the AI
  may keep acting.

```md docs/features/browser-use.md
# Browser use and co-browsing

> Browser sessions are the `kind="browser"` case of
> [co-desktops](/features/computer-use). The same manager, control lease
> and activity trail now also drive Linux desktops, Windows/macOS VMs and remote
> VNC/SSH machines.

Browser use gives every chat a real Chromium browser that **you and the AI
share**. It is not an AI-only headless browser and not a second "user browser":
there is one page, one history, one cookie jar and one live view.

## What you can do

- Open a browser session from **Co-desktops** or from a chat and watch the
  page live while the AI works.
- Click, type, scroll and navigate directly in the live view; the AI sees the
  same page on its next tool call.
- Ask the AI to navigate, click, fill forms, run JavaScript, read the page text,
  list links, take screenshots, inspect the HTML source, or review what the user
  did recently.
- Hand control back and forth explicitly. The AI pauses when the human types or
  clicks in the live view, and can request a handoff for login/MFA/captcha.
- Keep the browser profile (cookies, logins, local storage) across restarts.
- Save and replay per-site scripts in one tool call instead of one LLM turn per
  step.

## Architecture

```text
                   codx-junior_default Docker network
 ┌────────────────────┐        CDP (port 9223)        ┌──────────────────────┐
 │  API / SmolAgent   │ ────────────────────────────► │  Chromium container  │
 │  Playwright        │                               │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 └─────────┬──────────┘                               │  │ CDP proxy      │  │
           │                                          │  │ 9223 → 9222    │  │
           │ REST / Socket.IO                         │  └────────────────┘  │
 ┌─────────▼──────────┐      Traefik route            │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 │  User browser      │ ────────────────────────────► │  │ Selkies VNC    │  │
 │  live view iframe  │      /browser/<id>/           │  │ port 3000      │  │
 └────────────────────┘                               │  └────────────────┘  │
                                                      └──────────────────────┘
```

- **User control / viewing** — the LinuxServer.io Chromium image exposes a
  Selkies web desktop. Traefik routes it at `/browser/<session_id>/`; the
  session is configured with `SUBFOLDER` so all assets and websockets work
  behind the path prefix.
- **AI control** — Chromium binds DevTools to `127.0.0.1` and rejects non-local
  `Host` headers. A tiny in-container proxy (`cdp_proxy.py`) listens on
  `0.0.0.0:9223`, rewrites the header and tunnels the connection to
  `127.0.0.1:9222`. Playwright connects to the proxy over the shared Docker
  network; both actors therefore drive the **same page**.
- **Persistence** — the container mounts
  `.codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/chromium_profile` at `/config`.
- **Runtime** — the API keeps one Playwright connection per session (idle
  disconnect after 5 minutes) and serializes actions with a per-session lock.
  A 1-second watcher drains the in-page recorder, so human clicks/edits/tab
  switches show up as `actor=user` activity without polling the whole log.
- **Navigation** — `domcontentloaded` plus a short best-effort `load` wait;
  `networkidle` is no longer used (it timed out on live sites and the old code
  navigated a second time).

## Using it

### From the UI

Open **Co-desktops**, create a browser session with a name and optional start URL,
then select it. The live browser is embedded in the panel:

- address bar, back, forward and refresh send actions through the REST API;
- clicking and typing in the iframe controls the browser directly;
- the control badge shows who is driving (`AI`, `You active`, `You drive`);
  **Take control** pauses the AI and **Give back** resumes it;
- a handoff banner appears when the AI needs the human (login/MFA/captcha);
  complete it and click **I'm done — give back to AI**;
- the **Ask AI** button sends the current URL, title, selected text and active
  field to the browser chat;
- the **Shared activity** panel shows `User`, `AI` and `System` actions live
  (click/fill/submit/scroll/tab switch included);
- the **AI cost** panel shows the SmolAgent token usage and cxjcoins of every
  chat linked to the session;
- the session list on the left can be collapsed with the chevron on its edge,
  giving the live browser and chat more room (the state is remembered);
- **Chat** at the bottom opens the chat picker: choose an existing chat,
  open one of the chats already linked to the session, or click **New chat** to
  create one. The chat gets the `browser` profile and shares the page with the
  live view, so you can ask the AI to act on what you are watching without
  leaving the screen.

### From a chat

Browser tools are available to the agent by default (`browser` tools):

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `start_session` | Start or resume the chat's shared browser. Returns `session_id` and the live-view URL. |
| `browse_action` | `navigate`, `click`, `fill`, `execute`, `text`, `links`, `snapshot`, `back`, `forward`, `refresh`, `wait`, `press`, `select`, `hover`, `scroll`, tabs, and `batch` (several steps in one call). Click/fill by `ref` from a snapshot or by selector/text. |
| `browser_status` | Connection, URL/title, tabs and who controls the page. |
| `browser_control` | `status`, `handoff`, `take_control`, `give_back`, `pause`. |
| `get_screenshot` | Capture the current page (the user sees the image inline). |
| `get_source_code` | Return the page HTML (capped to keep model context small). |
| `browser_activity` | Recent user/AI actions, so the AI notices manual changes; supports `actor` and `since` filters. |
| `list_browser_scripts` / `get_browser_script` | Find/read a saved recipe. |
| `run_browser_script` | Execute a whole saved recipe in one call, on one connection. |
| `save_browser_script` / `delete_browser_script` | Maintain the per-site library (versioned, soft delete). |
| `finish_session` | Stop (or delete) the session, keeping the Chromium profile. |

The running chat id is injected automatically into these tools, so a session
started by the AI is linked to the chat the user is looking at.

## Auditing and cost

- Every user/AI action is appended to
  `.codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/activity.jsonl` with timestamp, actor,
  action, parameters, URL, title, duration and result/error. Input values are
  redacted (`value_redacted` + `value_length`) so passwords never land in the
  audit trail. The endpoint tail-reads the file and pushes new entries over
  Socket.IO (`codx-junior-browser-activity`).
- The in-page recorder captures human clicks, edits, submits, Enter keys, scrolls
  and tab switches. It tags AI-dispatched events so they are not attributed to
  the human.
- SmolAgent records token usage and cxjcoins through the existing analytics
  pipeline (`/api/browsers/{id}/cost` reconciles with the chat cost header).
- Tool calls are also archived by SmolAgent's tool-usage analytics, including
  the action, arguments and result.

## Co-browsing protocol

Control is explicit:

```text
ai_driving --user clicks/types--> user_active (AI yields)
user_active --10 s idle--> ai_driving
ai_driving --handoff(login/MFA/captcha)--> user_control (AI paused)
user_control --"I'm done" / Give back--> ai_driving
```

- `POST /api/browsers/{id}/control` (`take_control`, `give_back`, `pause`,
  `handoff`, `status`) moves the lease; the UI shows a control badge and a
  handoff banner.
- The AI must call `browser_activity(actor="user")` after a pause and must not
  act while `controller="user"` or the user is recently active.
- Before clicking, the AI can use refs from `browse_action(action="snapshot")`
  so the target is stable and the page shows what was clicked.
- The page recorder is installed in every tab; when the human switches tabs in
  the VNC view, the runtime follows the visible tab and logs `switch_tab`.

## Performance notes

- One Playwright connection per session removes the old ~0.45–0.55 s
  connect/disconnect cost per tool call (measured; subsequent actions are
  ~10–20 ms of overhead).
- `run_browser_script` executes a 20-step recipe in one LLM turn and one
  connection.
- Session create/stop/delete run off the API event loop; delete uses
  `docker rm -f` and moves the profile to `.trash` before deleting it.
- Activity is tail-read and pushed over Socket.IO; the UI polls only as a
  fallback every 15 s, and cost is refreshed at most once a minute.
- Script metadata lives in `meta.json` (the old `script.json` collided with the
  `steps` code file, which made saved recipes load empty).

## Requirements and notes

- The Chromium image is large (~2 GB compressed). The first session may take a
  while if the image is not cached; `CODX_BROWSER_AUTO_PULL=0` disables pulling.
- One container per session; the live view and the API must share the Docker
  network so the CDP proxy is reachable.
- The browser runs headful inside the container so the user's VNC view and the
  AI's automation share the exact same rendering surface.

async def tidy_blank_tabs(browser) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Close the empty tabs that accumulate when navigations fail.

    Opening a tab and failing to navigate leaves an ``about:blank`` behind; a
    session used for a couple of days ends up with a tab strip full of them (20
    blank tabs over 22 has been observed). This pass removes them while keeping
    everything that matters:

    - the keep-alive tab (it protects the browser window),
    - the tab the AI drives and the user is watching,
    - every tab that rendered something.

    It only acts when at least :data:`BLANK_TAB_THRESHOLD` blank tabs are open,
    so a tab the user has just created is never stolen, and never closes more
    than :data:`MAX_TIDY_CLOSES` in one pass.

    Args:
        browser: Connected :class:`Browser`.

    Returns:
        Dict[str, Any]: ``closed`` (how many were closed), ``blank`` (how many
        were found) and ``threshold``.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When the browser is not connected.

    Example:
        >>> await tidy_blank_tabs(browser)  # doctest: +SKIP
        {'closed': 6, 'blank': 6, 'threshold': 3}
    """
    pages = open_pages(browser)
    active = getattr(browser, "page", None)
    candidates = [
        page for page in pages
        if page is not active and is_blank_page(page)
    ]
    if len(candidates) < BLANK_TAB_THRESHOLD:
        return {"closed": 0, "blank": len(candidates), "threshold": BLANK_TAB_THRESHOLD}

    closed = 0
    for page in candidates[:MAX_TIDY_CLOSES]:
        try:
            await page.close()
            closed += 1
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Could not close a blank tab: %s", ex)

    if closed:
        logger.info(
            "Closed %s blank tab(s) of session %s (%s left)",
            closed, _session_label(browser), len(candidates) - closed,
        )
    return {
        "closed": closed,
        "blank": len(candidates),
        "threshold": BLANK_TAB_THRESHOLD,

```py api/codx/junior/browser/browser_manager.py
"""
BrowserManager / ComputerManager — CRUD and lifecycle for computer sessions.

A session is a machine shared by the user and the AI.  ``kind="browser"`` keeps
the original Chromium/CDP behaviour; ``linux`` runs a desktop container driven
through ``docker exec``; ``windows``/``macos`` run QEMU VMs driven through VNC;
``remote`` points at an existing VNC/SSH machine.  This class owns session
persistence, chat linking, activity audit, folder sharing and the per-session
runtime (BrowserRuntime for browsers, DesktopRuntime for desktops).

Follows the workspace pattern:
    .codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/<session_id>.session

A session is created with a human-readable ``name`` and may be shared by several
chats (``session.chat_ids``).  The container is a Chromium instance with a live
VNC view (for the user) and a CDP endpoint (for the AI), so both actors control
the same browser page.

Folder sharing
--------------
Any number of project folders are mounted inside the browser container under a
single tree (``/home/<project_name>/<folder>``) and the browser downloads are
written inside a project folder, so the user and the AI exchange files with the
project instead of being locked in the container:

- ``configure_share`` decides the mounts when the session is created;
- the downloads folder is written into the browser profile *before* the container
  starts (``codx/junior/browser/download_settings.py``), because Chromium reads
  the download directory at launch — this is the durable half and covers the
  downloads the user starts in the live VNC view;
- the same folder is also applied through CDP on every connection
  (``Browser.setDownloadBehavior``), which is the live half: it also covers a
  download triggered by the AI while its connection is open;
- ``get_shared_paths`` / ``get_shared_files`` expose the mapping and the files
  the browser saved inside the project.

Browser window survival
-----------------------
Chromium exits when its last window (tab) is closed, while the container keeps
running: the live view stays up but the browser window is gone and the DevTools
endpoint is dead.  Two defences keep a session usable:

- a protected **keep-alive tab** is created with the session and ensured on every
  connection (``codx/junior/browser/tabs.py``), so closing every other tab leaves
  the window alive;
- ``connect_browser`` **recovers** a dead browser by restarting the container
  entrypoint (which relaunches Chromium with the mounted profile) and retrying
  the connection once.

Lifecycle primitives
--------------------
- ``create_session(name, chat_id, initial_url, description)`` : start a new container + persist metadata.
- ``stop_session(session_id)``      : stop the container but KEEP it (restartable).
- ``restart_session(session_id)``   : relaunch Chromium (recovery) / recreate a stopped session.
- ``delete_session(session_id)``    : stop the container, remove it and the folder.
- ``log_activity(...)``             : append an audit entry for a user/AI action.
"""

def get_browser_manager(settings: CODXJuniorSettings) -> "BrowserManager":

def _is_inside(path: str, base: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *path* is inside *base* (both may be relative)."""
    try:
        return os.path.commonpath(
            [os.path.abspath(path), os.path.abspath(base)]
        ) == os.path.abspath(base)
    except ValueError:
        return False

    """
    Schedule *coroutine* on the running loop, keeping a reference until it ends.

    Used for work that must never block a request (creating the keep-alive tab).
    """
    task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(coroutine)
    _background_tasks.add(task)
    task.add_done_callback(_background_tasks.discard)

            share_folders: Project folders mounted under
                ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>``. Each entry is a project
                relative path or a dict with folder/name/mount_path/readonly.
            readonly: Mount the listed folders read-only.
            downloads_folder: Project-relative folder receiving the downloads
                (default ``.codx/browser_downloads/<session_id>``).
            downloads_mount: Container path forcing a dedicated downloads mount.
            kind: ``browser`` (default), ``linux``, ``windows``, ``macos`` or
                ``remote``.  See :class:`BrowserSession`.
            os_version: OS release for VM images (Windows 11, macOS 15...).
            image: Docker image override (container kinds).
            image_provider: linuxserver, kasmweb or custom. Inferred from
                ``image`` when omitted.
            library_item_id: Start from a saved computer in the project library.
                The saved image/live-view/defaults take precedence over
                ``image``/``image_provider``.
            vnc_host: Remote VNC host (``remote`` kind; also inferred for VMs).
            vnc_port: Remote VNC port (default 5900).
            vnc_password: Remote VNC password.
            vnc_public_url: Optional viewer URL supplied by the user.
            ssh_host/ssh_port/ssh_user/ssh_key_path/ssh_password: Optional SSH
                endpoint used by ``run_command`` on remote sessions.
            guest_share_path: Where the shared folder appears in a VM guest.
            control: Force a control channel (normally inferred from ``kind``).
            cpu_cores: vCPUs for the machine (advanced settings).
            ram_size: RAM size for the machine, e.g. ``"8G"`` (advanced).
            disk_size: Disk size for a Windows/macOS VM image, e.g. ``"64G"``.
            shm_size: Docker shared memory for browser/Linux containers.
            extra_env: Extra environment variables passed to the image.
            desktop_width/desktop_height: Desktop/browser window size in pixels.

        Returns:
            Created BrowserSession

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If container startup fails
            ValueError: If a folder is outside the project or missing
        """
        existing_sessions = self.list_sessions()
        if len(existing_sessions) >= self.docker_manager.MAX_SESSIONS:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Maximum number of browser sessions reached "
                f"({self.docker_manager.MAX_SESSIONS}); delete an old session first."
            )

        from codx.junior.browser.model import normalize_kind
        from codx.junior.computer.images import resolve_image
        from codx.junior.computer.library import (
            restore_profile,
            saved_library_for,
        )

        session_kind = normalize_kind(kind)
        image = (image or "").strip() or None
        image_provider = (image_provider or "").strip().lower() or None
        image_spec = None
        library_item = None
        library = None
        if library_item_id:
            library = saved_library_for(self)
            library_item = library.get(library_item_id)
            if not library_item:
                raise ValueError("Saved computer not found")
            if library_item.kind != "linux":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Saved computer kind '{library_item.kind}' is not supported for new sessions"
                )
            session_kind = normalize_kind(library_item.kind)
            image = library_item.image
            image_provider = library_item.provider
            # Apply the saved resource/env shape only where the caller did not
            # provide an explicit value.
            defaults = library_item.defaults or {}
            cpu_cores = cpu_cores if cpu_cores is not None else defaults.get("cpu_cores")
            ram_size = ram_size if ram_size is not None else defaults.get("ram_size")
            disk_size = disk_size if disk_size is not None else defaults.get("disk_size")
            shm_size = shm_size if shm_size is not None else defaults.get("shm_size")
            desktop_width = desktop_width or defaults.get("desktop_width")
            desktop_height = desktop_height or defaults.get("desktop_height")
            extra_env = {
                **(defaults.get("extra_env") or {}),
                **(extra_env or {}),
            }
        elif session_kind == "linux":
            # Resolve before creating the record: the image decides the live
            # view (Selkies/KasmVNC), its port/scheme and the Docker profile.
            image_spec = resolve_image(
                image or os.environ.get("CODX_COMPUTER_LINUX_IMAGE"),
                provider=image_provider,
                kind=session_kind,
            )
            image = image_spec.image
        session = BrowserSession(
            name=name,
            description=(description or "").strip() or None,
            chat_ids=[chat_id] if chat_id else [],
            current_url=(initial_url or "").strip() or None,
            kind=session_kind,
            os_version=(os_version or "").strip() or None,
            image=(image or "").strip() or None,
            control=(control or "").strip().lower() or None,
            vnc_host=(vnc_host or "").strip() or None,
            vnc_port=int(vnc_port or 5900),
            vnc_password=vnc_password or None,
            vnc_public_url=(vnc_public_url or "").strip() or None,
            ssh_host=(ssh_host or "").strip() or None,
            ssh_port=int(ssh_port or 22),
            ssh_user=(ssh_user or "").strip() or None,
            ssh_key_path=(ssh_key_path or "").strip() or None,
            ssh_password=ssh_password or None,
            guest_share_path=(guest_share_path or "").strip() or None,
            cpu_cores=cpu_cores,
            ram_size=(ram_size or "").strip() or None,
            disk_size=(disk_size or "").strip() or None,
            shm_size=(shm_size or "").strip() or None,
            extra_env=extra_env or {},
            desktop_width=desktop_width or 1920,
            desktop_height=desktop_height or 1080,
        )
        if image_spec is not None:
            session.image = image_spec.image
            session.image_provider = image_spec.provider
            session.live_view = image_spec.live_view
            session.live_port = image_spec.live_port
            session.live_scheme = image_spec.live_scheme
            session.strip_prefix = image_spec.strip_prefix
            session.viewer_user = image_spec.viewer_user
            if image_spec.provider == "kasmweb" and not session.viewer_password:
                session.viewer_password = secrets.token_urlsafe(9)
        if library_item is not None:
            session.library_item_id = library_item.id
            session.library_item_name = library_item.name
            session.image = library_item.image
            session.image_provider = library_item.provider
            session.live_view = library_item.live_view
            session.live_port = library_item.live_port
            session.live_scheme = library_item.live_scheme
            session.strip_prefix = bool(library_item.strip_prefix)
            session.control = library_item.control or session.control
            session.viewer_user = library_item.viewer_user
            if (library_item.provider or "").lower() == "kasmweb" and not session.viewer_password:
                session.viewer_password = secrets.token_urlsafe(9)
        if session.ssh_host and "shell" not in (session.capabilities or []):
            session.capabilities = [*(session.capabilities or []), "shell"]
        if not session.name:
            session.name = f"{session.kind_label} {session.id[:8]}"

        session_folder = self._session_folder_path(session.id)
        os.makedirs(session_folder, exist_ok=True)

        if session.kind == "remote":
            if not session.vnc_host:
                raise ValueError("Remote computer sessions require vnc_host")
            session.status = "running"
            session.vnc_url = session.vnc_public_url
            session.engine = "remote"
            session.control = "vnc"
            session.mark_active()
            self._save_session_file(session)
            self.log_activity(
                session,
                actor="system",
                action="create",
                chat_id=chat_id,
                params={
                    "kind": "remote",
                    "vnc": f"{session.vnc_host}:{session.vnc_port}",
                    "ssh": session.ssh_host or None,
                },
            )
            return session

        # The project folders (and the downloads folder) must be mapped before
        # the container is created: docker run mounts them.
        self.docker_manager.configure_share(
            session,
            share_project=share_project,
            share_folders=share_folders,
            readonly=readonly,
            downloads_folder=downloads_folder,
            downloads_mount=downloads_mount,
        )

        if session.kind == "browser":
            # Chromium reads its download directory at launch, so the mapped
            # folder must reach the profile *before* the container is created.
            self._prepare_downloads(session)

        if library_item is not None and library_item.has_profile and library is not None:
            profile_path = self.docker_manager._desktop_profile_path(session.id)
            try:
                restore_profile(library_item, library, profile_path)
            except Exception:
                # Never leave a half-created session behind.
                self.delete_session(session.id)
                raise

        logger.info(
            "Creating %s session %s ('%s') for chat %s",
            session.kind, session.id[:8], session.name, chat_id,
        )

        # Start Docker container (browser or desktop/VM)
        session = self.docker_manager.start_container(session)

        # The keep-alive tab and the page recorder are ensured by the runtime
        # on its first connection: doing it here would open a second Playwright
        # connection (and add ~0.5 s) before the session is even returned.

        # Save session metadata to file
        self._save_session_file(session)
        self.log_activity(
            session,
            actor="system",
            action="create",
            chat_id=chat_id,
            params={
                "name": session.name,
                "initial_url": initial_url,
                "folders": [share.mount_path for share in session.shared_folders],
                "downloads": session.downloads_mount,
            },
            url=session.current_url,
            title=session.current_title,
        )
        return session

    def update_session(
        self,
        session_id: str,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        description: Optional[str] = None,
        control: Optional[str] = None,
        vnc_host: Optional[str] = None,
        vnc_port: Optional[int] = None,
        vnc_password: Optional[str] = None,
        vnc_public_url: Optional[str] = None,
        ssh_host: Optional[str] = None,
        ssh_port: Optional[int] = None,
        ssh_user: Optional[str] = None,
        ssh_key_path: Optional[str] = None,
        ssh_password: Optional[str] = None,
        advanced: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> Optional[BrowserSession]:
        """
        Update a session (name, connection and advanced settings) and persist it.

        ``vnc_password``/``ssh_password`` are changed when the field is not
        ``None``; pass ``""`` to clear them.  This lets a session be created
        first (e.g. a VM that needs to boot) and get its SSH endpoint later
        without recreating it.

        ``advanced`` holds the image/resource fields (``image``, ``cpu_cores``,
        ``ram_size``, ``disk_size``, ``shm_size``, ``extra_env``,
        ``desktop_width``/``desktop_height``).  Docker cannot change those on a
        running container: they take effect when the session is restarted
        (the container is recreated and the VM disk/profile is preserved).

        Returns:
            The updated BrowserSession, or None when not found.
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if not session:
            return None
        if name is not None and str(name).strip():
            session.name = str(name).strip()
        if description is not None:
            session.description = str(description).strip() or None
        if control is not None and str(control).strip():
            from codx.junior.browser.model import CONTROL_MODES
            value = str(control).strip().lower()
            if value not in CONTROL_MODES:
                raise ValueError(f"control must be one of: {', '.join(CONTROL_MODES)}")
            session.control = value
        if vnc_host is not None:
            session.vnc_host = str(vnc_host).strip() or None
        if vnc_port is not None:
            session.vnc_port = int(vnc_port)
        if vnc_password is not None:
            session.vnc_password = str(vnc_password) or None
        if vnc_public_url is not None:
            session.vnc_public_url = str(vnc_public_url).strip() or None
        if ssh_host is not None:
            session.ssh_host = str(ssh_host).strip() or None
        if ssh_port is not None:
            session.ssh_port = int(ssh_port)
        if ssh_user is not None:
            session.ssh_user = str(ssh_user).strip() or None
        if ssh_key_path is not None:
            session.ssh_key_path = str(ssh_key_path).strip() or None
        if ssh_password is not None:
            session.ssh_password = str(ssh_password) or None
        if session.ssh_host and "shell" not in (session.capabilities or []):
            session.capabilities = [*(session.capabilities or []), "shell"]
        if advanced:
            session.apply_advanced_settings(advanced)
            if "image" in advanced:
                # Editing the image detaches the session from a saved-library
                # item; it should no longer be treated as a saved snapshot.
                session.library_item_id = None
                session.library_item_name = None
            if session.kind == "linux" and "image" in advanced:
                # The image decides the live-view transport (Selkies vs
                # KasmVNC): re-resolve it so a changed/cleared override does
                # not keep the previous provider's ports and scheme.
                from codx.junior.computer.images import resolve_image
                spec = resolve_image(
                    session.image or os.environ.get("CODX_COMPUTER_LINUX_IMAGE"),
                    kind="linux",
                )
                session.image = spec.image
                session.image_provider = spec.provider
                session.live_view = spec.live_view
                session.live_port = spec.live_port
                session.live_scheme = spec.live_scheme
                session.strip_prefix = spec.strip_prefix
                session.viewer_user = spec.viewer_user
                if spec.provider == "kasmweb":
                    session.viewer_password = session.viewer_password or secrets.token_urlsafe(9)
                else:
                    session.viewer_password = None
        session.mark_active()
        self._save_session_file(session)
        # Extra image env values can contain credentials: audit the names only.
        safe_advanced = {
            key: (sorted(value) if key == "extra_env" and isinstance(value, dict) else value)
            for key, value in (advanced or {}).items()
        }
        self.log_activity(
            session,
            actor="system",
            action="update",
            params={"name": session.name, **safe_advanced},
        )
        return session

    def save_session(self, session: BrowserSession) -> BrowserSession:
        """
        Create or update a session.

        Args:
            session: BrowserSession to save

        Returns:
            The saved session object
        """
        session_folder = self._session_folder_path(session.id)
        os.makedirs(session_folder, exist_ok=True)

        logger.debug("Saving session '%s'", session.id[:8])
        self._save_session_file(session)

        return session

    def connect_chat(self, session_id: str, chat_id: str) -> Optional[BrowserSession]:
        """
        Connect an additional chat to an existing session.

        Args:
            session_id: Session to connect the chat to.
            chat_id: Chat ID to connect.

        Returns:
            The updated BrowserSession, or None when the session is not found.
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if not session:
            logger.warning("connect_chat: session not found: %s", session_id)
            return None
        session.add_chat(chat_id)
        self._save_session_file(session)
        logger.info("Connected chat %s to session %s", chat_id, session.id[:8])
        return session

    def stop_session(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[BrowserSession]:
        """
        Stop a session's container but KEEP it so it can be restarted.

        Args:
            session_id: Session ID to stop

        Returns:
            The updated BrowserSession, or None when not found.
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if not session:
            logger.warning("stop_session: session not found: %s", session_id)
            return None

        self.forget_runtime(session_id)
        if session.kind != "remote":
            # VMs need a graceful shutdown so the guest disk is consistent;
            # browser/Linux containers keep the historic fast stop call.
            if session.kind in ("windows", "macos"):
                self.docker_manager.stop_container(session, remove=False, fast=False)
            else:
                self.docker_manager.stop_container(session, remove=False)
        else:
            session.status = "stopped"
        self._save_session_file(session)
        self.log_activity(session, actor="system", action="stop")
        logger.info("Stopped session %s", session_id[:8])
        return session

    def delete_session(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        """
        Stop container, remove it and delete the session folder.

        Args:
            session_id: Session ID to delete
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if session:
            # Stop & remove Docker container (fast kill: no 10 s grace period)
            self.log_activity(session, actor="system", action="delete")
            if session.kind != "remote":
                self.docker_manager.stop_container(session, remove=True)
                logger.info("Stopped container for session %s", session_id[:8])

        self.forget_runtime(session_id)

        # Deleting a 100+ MB Chromium profile with shutil.rmtree() on the event
        # loop makes the whole API stutter.  Move it to .trash (same filesystem,
        # instant) and let the caller/background cleanup remove it.
        session_folder = self._session_folder_path(session_id)
        if os.path.isdir(session_folder):
            trash = os.path.join(self.sessions_path, ".trash")
            try:
                os.makedirs(trash, exist_ok=True)
                target = os.path.join(
                    trash, f"{session_id}-{int(time.time())}"
                )
                shutil.move(session_folder, target)
                logger.info("Moved session folder to trash: %s", session_id[:8])
                threading.Thread(
                    target=self._remove_trash_folder, args=(target,), daemon=True
                ).start()
            except Exception as e:
                logger.exception("Error moving session folder to trash: %s", e)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Project folder sharing
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_shared_paths(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the project/downloads mapping of a session.

        Args:
            session_id: Session ID

        Returns:
            Dict with ``session_id``, ``project_name``, ``home_path``,
            ``folders`` (list of share dicts), ``downloads_path``,
            ``downloads_folder``, ``downloads_mount`` and
            ``downloads_own_mount``; or None when the session does not exist.
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if not session:
            return None
        return {
            "session_id": session.id,
            "project_name": session.project_name,
            "home_path": session.home_path,
            "folders": [share.to_dict() for share in session.shared_folders],
            "downloads_path": session.downloads_path,
            "downloads_folder": session.downloads_folder,
            "downloads_mount": session.downloads_mount,
            "downloads_own_mount": bool(session.downloads_own_mount),
        }

    def get_shared_files(self, session_id: str, limit: int = 200) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        List the files the browser saved in the session's downloads folder.

        The folder lives inside the project when the project is shared, so every
        entry can be read through the project files API.

        Args:
            session_id: Session ID
            limit: Maximum number of entries (newest first)

        Returns:
            List of dicts with ``name``, ``relative_path``, ``path``,
            ``container_path``, ``size`` and ``modified_at``.
        """
        session = self.get_session(session_id)
        if not session or not session.downloads_path:
            return []
        root = session.downloads_path
        if not os.path.isdir(root):
            return []

        project_root = getattr(self.settings, "abs_project_path", None)
        project_root = project_root if isinstance(project_root, str) and project_root else None
        downloads_mount = (session.downloads_mount or "").rstrip("/")

        files: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        for folder, _subfolders, names in os.walk(root):
            for name in names:
                full_path = os.path.join(folder, name)
                # Chromium keeps the partial download next to the final file
                if name.endswith(".crdownload"):
                    continue
                try:
                    stat = os.stat(full_path)
                except OSError:
                    continue
                relative = os.path.relpath(full_path, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
                if project_root and _is_inside(full_path, project_root):
                    path = os.path.relpath(full_path, project_root).replace(os.sep, "/")
                else:
                    path = full_path
                files.append({
                    "name": name,
                    "relative_path": relative,
                    "path": path,
                    "container_path": f"{downloads_mount}/{relative}" if downloads_mount else relative,
                    "size": int(stat.st_size),
                    "modified_at": datetime.utcfromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime).isoformat(),
                })

        files.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["modified_at"], reverse=True)
        return files[:max(1, min(int(limit or 200), MAX_SHARED_FILES))]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Chat integration
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    def get_session_from_chat(self, chat: "Chat") -> Optional[BrowserSession]:
        """
        Load a browser session from Chat.meta_data.

        Args:
            chat: Chat object

        Returns:
            BrowserSession or None if not in chat metadata
        """
        if not getattr(chat, "meta_data", None) or "browser" not in chat.meta_data:
            return None

        try:
            session_data = chat.meta_data["browser"]
            return BrowserSession.from_dict(session_data)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Error loading session from chat: %s", e)
            return None

    def save_session_to_chat(self, session: BrowserSession, chat: "Chat") -> None:
        """
        Save session to Chat.meta_data["browser"] and connect the chat to it.

        Several chats can be connected to the same session: every call registers
        the chat in ``session.chat_ids`` (persisted to the session file) in
        addition to storing the session snapshot in the chat metadata.

        Args:
            session: BrowserSession to save
            chat: Chat to update
        """
        if getattr(chat, "meta_data", None) is None:
            chat.meta_data = {}

        # Register this chat as a consumer of the shared session
        if getattr(chat, "id", None):
            session.add_chat(chat.id)
            self._save_session_file(session)

        chat.meta_data["browser"] = session.to_public_dict()
        logger.debug("Saved session %s to chat %s", session.id[:8], chat.id)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Persistent runtimes
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def get_runtime(self, session: BrowserSession):
        """Return (creating once) the persistent runtime of *session*.

        Browser sessions get a Playwright/``BrowserRuntime``; desktop sessions
        get a ``DesktopRuntime`` backed by ``docker exec`` (Linux) or RFB
        (Windows/macOS/remote).  Both are cached per session and expose the same
        ``run``/``close``/``loop`` surface used by the API and tools.
        """
        if getattr(self, "_runtimes_guard", None) is None:
            self._runtimes = {}
            self._runtimes_guard = threading.Lock()
        try:
            current_loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        except RuntimeError:
            current_loop = None
        with self._runtimes_guard:
            runtime = self._runtimes.get(session.id)
            stale_loop = (
                runtime is not None
                and getattr(runtime, "loop", None) is not None
                and current_loop is not None
                and runtime.loop is not current_loop
            )
            if runtime is None or getattr(runtime, "_closed", False) or stale_loop:
                if session.kind == "browser":
                    from codx.junior.browser.runtime import BrowserRuntime
                    runtime = BrowserRuntime(self, session)
                else:
                    from codx.junior.computer.runtime import DesktopRuntime
                    runtime = DesktopRuntime(self, session)
                runtime.loop = current_loop
                self._runtimes[session.id] = runtime
            return runtime

    async def warm_runtime(self, session: BrowserSession) -> None:
        """Connect the runtime in the background so human input is captured.

        A session created from the UI may be driven by the human before the AI
        says anything.  Connecting once here starts the page recorder and the
        1 s watcher, so those clicks appear in the activity trail immediately.
        """
        if session.kind != "browser":
            # Desktop backends connect lazily on the first action; there is no
            # page recorder that must be started in advance.
            return
        try:
            runtime = await self.get_runtime(session)
            await runtime.drain()
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.debug("Could not warm browser runtime %s: %s", str(session.id)[:8], ex)

    def peek_runtime(self, session_id: str):
        """Return the runtime without creating it (or None)."""
        return getattr(self, "_runtimes", {}).get(session_id)

    def forget_runtime(self, session_id: str) -> None:
        """Drop a session runtime and close it on the loop that owns it."""
        runtime = getattr(self, "_runtimes", {}).pop(session_id, None)
        if runtime is None:
            return
        loop = getattr(runtime, "loop", None)
        if loop is None or not loop.is_running():
            return
        try:
            current = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        except RuntimeError:
            current = None
        try:
            if current is loop:
                _spawn_background(runtime.close())
            elif loop.is_running():
                asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(runtime.close(), loop)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass

    def _remove_trash_folder(self, path: str) -> None:
        """Delete a trashed session folder off the request path."""
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)
            logger.info("Removed trashed session folder %s", path)
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("Could not remove trashed session folder %s: %s", path, ex)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Browser connection + keep-alive tab
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def connect_browser(self, session: BrowserSession) -> Browser:
        """
        Create a Browser instance, connect via CDP and prepare the shared page.

        Chromium exits when its last window is closed, which leaves the container
        running with a dead DevTools endpoint (the live view is still up but the
        browser window is gone).  A failed connection is therefore recovered once
        by restarting the browser process, so a session never stays unreachable,
        and the protected keep-alive tab is ensured on every connection.

        Args:
            session: BrowserSession with container info

        Returns:
            Connected Browser instance

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If connection fails, even after the recovery attempt
        """
        browser = Browser(session, self.docker_manager)
        try:
            await browser.connect()
        except Exception as ex:
            if not session.container_id:
                raise
            logger.warning(
                "Browser of session %s is not reachable (%s); restarting it",
                str(session.id)[:8], ex,
            )
            try:
                await browser.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
            session = await asyncio.to_thread(self._restart_browser, session)
            browser = Browser(session, self.docker_manager)
            await browser.connect()

        await self._apply_downloads_path(browser, session)
        await self._ensure_keep_alive_tab(browser, session)
        return browser

    def _prepare_downloads(self, session: BrowserSession) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Anchor the session's download folder in the browser profile.

        ``Browser.setDownloadBehavior`` (used by :meth:`_apply_downloads_path`)
        is scoped to the DevTools client that sends it and Chromium drops it when
        that client disconnects — which happens on every tool call — and it never
        applies to a download the user starts in the live VNC view.  The mapping
        must therefore also be stored where Chromium reads it at launch:

        - ``download.default_directory`` (+ ``savefile``) in the profile
          ``Preferences``, without a "save as" prompt;
        - ``<HOME>/Downloads`` (inside ``/config``, the mounted profile) pointing
          at the mapped folder, so the browser fallback lands there too.

        Must be called *before* the container starts.  Best effort: a session
        whose profile cannot be written still works, it only keeps the
        per-connection CDP mapping.

        Args:
            session: Session whose ``downloads_mount`` becomes the browser's
                download folder.

        Returns:
            Dict[str, Any]: Report from ``download_settings`` (empty when there
            is nothing to map or the profile could not be written).
        """
        if not session or not session.downloads_mount:
            return {}
        try:
            report = download_settings.apply_download_settings(
                self._profile_folder(session.id), session.downloads_mount
            )
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "Could not set the download folder of session %s: %s",
                str(session.id)[:8], ex,
            )
            return {}
        if report.get("preferences"):
            logger.info(
                "Session %s download folder: %s (%d preference file(s), link: %s)",
                str(session.id)[:8],
                session.downloads_mount,
                len(report["preferences"]),
                report.get("symlink") or "-",
            )
        return report

    async def _apply_downloads_path(self, browser: Browser, session: BrowserSession) -> None:
        """
        Point the running browser to the session's mapped download folder.

        This is the *live* half of the mapping: while the connection is open it
        also covers a download started by the AI (and it wins over anything
        Playwright sets for its own context).  Chromium scopes
        ``Browser.setDownloadBehavior`` to the DevTools client that sends it, so
        the value is dropped when the connection closes — the durable half lives
        in the profile (see :meth:`_prepare_downloads`).

        Args:
            browser: Connected Browser instance.
            session: Session whose ``downloads_mount`` is applied.
        """
        download_path = (session.downloads_mount or "").strip()
        if not download_path or not getattr(browser, "browser", None):
            return
        try:
            cdp_session = await browser.browser.new_browser_cdp_session()
            # Keep a strong reference: a detached CDP session resets the
            # behaviour being set right below.
            browser.downloads_cdp_session = cdp_session
            await cdp_session.send(
                "Browser.setDownloadBehavior",
                {
                    "behavior": "allow",
                    "downloadPath": download_path,
                    "eventsEnabled": False,
                },
            )
            logger.info(
                "Browser downloads pointed to %s (session %s)",
                download_path, str(session.id)[:8],

        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "Could not point the browser downloads to %s: %s "
                "(the profile default written when the session was created still applies)",
                download_path, ex,
