"""
Tests for the tab-strip hygiene: blank tabs and failed navigations.

Opening a tab and failing to navigate leaves an ``about:blank`` behind, so a
session used for a couple of days ended up with a tab strip full of them (20
blank tabs over 22 was observed in production). These tests drive the tab layer
with fake Playwright pages, so no browser is needed.
"""

import asyncio

import pytest

from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs


class _FakeSession:
    """Minimal BrowserSession stand-in (only the fields the tab layer touches)."""

    def __init__(self, current_url=None):
        self.id = "12345678-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-ddddeeeeffff"
        self.current_url = current_url
        self.current_title = None

    def mark_active(self):
        pass


class _FakePage:
    def __init__(self, url="about:blank", title="", context=None):
        self.url = url
        self._title = title
        self._closed = False
        self.context = context

    async def title(self):
        return self._title

    def is_closed(self):
        return self._closed

    async def bring_to_front(self):
        pass

    async def close(self):
        self._closed = True
        if self.context and self in self.context.pages:
            self.context.pages.remove(self)


class _FakeContext:
    def __init__(self, pages=None):
        self.pages = list(pages or [])

    async def new_page(self):
        page = _FakePage(context=self)
        self.pages.append(page)
        return page


class _FakeBrowser:
    """Connected Browser double; ``navigate`` fails for a URL containing "boom"."""

    def __init__(self, pages=None):
        pages = list(pages) if pages else [_FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")]
        self.context = _FakeContext(pages)
        for page in pages:
            page.context = self.context
        self.page = pages[0]
        self.session = _FakeSession(current_url="https://a.test")

    async def navigate(self, url):
        if "boom" in url:
            raise RuntimeError(f"navigation to {url} failed")
        self.page.url = url
        return url


def _run(coroutine):
    return asyncio.run(coroutine)


def _blank_pages(count):
    return [_FakePage(url="about:blank") for _ in range(count)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tidy_blank_tabs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_blank_tabs_are_closed_and_the_working_tab_is_kept():
    working = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    keep_alive = _FakePage(url=browser_tabs.KEEP_ALIVE_URL, title=browser_tabs.KEEP_ALIVE_TITLE)
    blanks = _blank_pages(5)
    browser = _FakeBrowser([working, keep_alive, *blanks])

    result = _run(browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(browser))

    assert result["closed"] == 5
    assert result["blank"] == 5
    assert browser.context.pages == [working, keep_alive]
    assert browser.page is working
    assert not any(page.is_closed() for page in (working, keep_alive))


def test_one_or_two_blank_tabs_are_left_alone():
    working = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    blanks = _blank_pages(2)
    browser = _FakeBrowser([working, *blanks])

    result = _run(browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(browser))

    assert result["closed"] == 0
    assert result["threshold"] == browser_tabs.BLANK_TAB_THRESHOLD
    assert len(browser.context.pages) == 3
    assert not any(page.is_closed() for page in blanks)


def test_the_active_tab_is_never_closed_even_when_it_is_blank():
    blank_active = _FakePage(url="about:blank")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([blank_active, *_blank_pages(4)])
    browser.page = blank_active

    result = _run(browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(browser))

    assert result["closed"] == 4
    assert not blank_active.is_closed()
    assert browser.page is blank_active


def test_a_tidy_pass_is_capped():
    working = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    blanks = _blank_pages(browser_tabs.MAX_TIDY_CLOSES + 10)
    browser = _FakeBrowser([working, *blanks])

    result = _run(browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(browser))

    assert result["closed"] == browser_tabs.MAX_TIDY_CLOSES
    assert len(browser.context.pages) == 11


def test_tidy_requires_a_connected_browser():
    browser = _FakeBrowser()
    browser.context = None

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        _run(browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(browser))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# open_tab
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_open_tab_does_not_leave_a_blank_tab_when_the_navigation_fails():
    working = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([working])

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        _run(browser_tabs.open_tab(browser, "https://boom.test"))

    # The failed tab is gone and the previous one is active again
    assert browser.context.pages == [working]
    assert browser.page is working


def test_open_tab_opens_and_navigates():
    working = _FakePage(url="https://a.test", title="A")
    browser = _FakeBrowser([working])

    tab = _run(browser_tabs.open_tab(browser, "https://b.test"))

    assert tab["url"] == "https://b.test"
    assert tab["active"] is True
    assert len(browser.context.pages) == 2
    assert browser.page.url == "https://b.test"

"""Throwaway probe: run the real tidy pass against a live session (delete after use)."""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import urllib.request
from types import SimpleNamespace

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/codx-junior/codx-junior/api")

from codx.junior.browser import tabs as browser_tabs  # noqa: E402
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright  # noqa: E402


def ws_url(name):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://{name}:9223/json/version", timeout=10) as resp:
        version = json.load(resp)
    path = version["webSocketDebuggerUrl"].split("9222", 1)[-1]
    return f"ws://{name}:9223{path if path.startswith('/') else '/' + path}"


async def main(name):
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        driver = await p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(ws_url(name))
        context = driver.contexts[0]
        pages = list(context.pages)
        print("before:", len(pages))
        for page in pages:
            print("   ", page.url or "(empty)")
        active = next((pg for pg in reversed(pages) if pg.url and pg.url != "about:blank"), None)
        fake = SimpleNamespace(context=context, page=active, session=SimpleNamespace(id=name))
        print("tidy:", await browser_tabs.tidy_blank_tabs(fake))
        print("after:", len(context.pages))
        for page in context.pages:
            print("   ", page.url or "(empty)")
        await driver.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1]))

Let me stub the socket layer so the `ChatManager` lifecycle can still be verified offline:All 12 tests pass (10 storage + 2 full `ChatManager` lifecycle). Now the docs:Now removing the temporary runner and committing everything onto the PR worktree:Done — the feature is implemented, tested and committed on the isolated branch.

## What was built

**Storage** — `api/codx/junior/kanban/archive.py` (new): `TaskArchive` packs a task into `.codx/tasks/.archive/<chat_id>.tar.gz` (the chat JSON keeps its original file name inside the archive, so a restore needs no guessing) and keeps a metadata-only `index.json` (name, board, column, status, dates, sizes, `archived_by`). `fcntl` lock across processes, atomic index writes, compression to a `.tmp` then `os.replace`, and extraction that refuses members carrying a path.

**Invisible by default** — `.archive` is hidden and `is_store_file()` now rejects it, so `chat_paths()`, listings, `search_tasks`, analytics and cost roll-ups never see an archived task. `list_chats()` / `get_recent_chats()` (and `ChatManager`) gained `include_archived`, which merges the index as metadata-only `Chat` objects (`archived=True`) **without decompressing anything**.

**User path** — `POST /api/chats/archive`, `POST /api/chats/restore`, `GET /api/chats/archived` (+ `stats`), and `include_archived=true` on `GET /api/chats` and `/api/chats/recent`.

**Profile path** — `project_manager` gained `archive_task` / `restore_task` (plus aliases `archive`/`restore`/`unarchive`) and `list_tasks(include_archived=true)`, marked with 🗄️ in the table.

## Design decisions / what I discarded

| Option | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `tar.gz` per task | **Chosen** — keeps the original file name, streaming-friendly, one payload per task |
| `zip` per task or one big archive | Discarded: a per-board blob makes restoring a single task rewrite everything |
| "Archive = flag / move to a Done folder" | Discarded: the file stays parsed on every listing, so it saves zero space |
| Auto-archive policy (age-based) | Not built — separate decision, natural next step for the board manager |

## Verification

`api/tests/test_task_archive.py` → **12/12 pass** in the container: 10 storage tests (compress + remove live file, idempotency, byte-identical restore, traversal-safe extraction, forget, stats, `is_store_file`) and 2 end-to-end `ChatManager` lifecycle tests (task visible → archived and hidden from `list_chats` *and* `get_recent_chats` → visible with `include_archived` → restored with its conversation). Two of my first drafts failed and found real bugs, now fixed: `archive()` was not idempotent, and `_extract` accepted path-bearing members.

  boards/<board_id>/board.json     { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,folder,order,project_id,profiles}] }
  <folder>/<column_folder>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json
```

``folder`` is **immutable**: it is the name of the directory that holds the
board/column chats. ``title`` is only a label, so renaming a board or a column
changes nothing on disk and no task has to be rewritten.

Columns may additionally declare the defaults of the tasks created in them
(see :meth:`codx.junior.kanban.store.KanbanStore.column_defaults`):

* ``project_id`` - the TARGET project those tasks work on (the file keeps

A **task** is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in

every entry point behaves exactly the same.

Creation rules
--------------
1. **Only two kinds of callers may create tasks**: the LLM tools
   (``create_task`` and ``project_manager(action="create_task")``) and the API
   endpoints (``POST /api/chats/tasks``). Both delegate here.
2. **All the information must come from the caller.** ``name`` and
   ``description`` are mandatory: there is no AI step that expands, splits or
   rewrites a task after creation.
3. **Nothing is inherited from the parent chat.** ``profiles``, ``files``,
   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the

This module is responsible for chat persistence and management.

Besides the classic full-chat ``save_chat``, this module now exposes granular,
merge-safe message operations (``add_message``, ``update_message``,
``remove_message``) used to persist chat changes *during* an AI turn (e.g.
tool-usage notification messages, streamed partial responses) without
overwriting concurrent updates.

It also provides full-text search capabilities via the ``search_chats`` method,
delegating to the ``ChatSearcher`` class for filtering by time frame, keyword
matching, and pagination.

Merge strategy (per message, keyed by ``doc_id``):

    flowchart TD

        B[Stored chat messages] --> C
        C -->|No| D[Keep message]
        C -->|Yes| E{parse incoming.updated_at >= parse stored.updated_at?}
        E -->|Yes| F[Keep incoming]
        E -->|No| G[Keep stored]
        D --> H[Merged message list]

"""
Collection change events — keep every connected client in sync.

A **collection** is any server-side set of items a client caches in its store:
the project list, the profiles of a project, the teams, the kanban boards…
When one of those items is created, updated or deleted, answering the caller of
the REST endpoint is not enough: every OTHER client (another browser tab,
another user, the same user in the desktop shell) keeps rendering its cached
copy and only sees the change after a manual reload.

This module is the single place that announces those changes. One Socket.IO
event — :data:`COLLECTION_EVENT` — carries the collection, the action and the
affected item::

    {
      "collection": "profiles",
      "action": "upserted",
      "item": { "name": "reviewer" },
      "codx_path": "/projects/acme/.codx",
      "project_id": "3f1c…",
      "project_name": "acme",
      "source": "profile_manager",
      "ts": 1712345678
    }

Clients subscribe **once** and reload only the collection named in the payload
(see ``client/src/store/collections.js``). The REST endpoints stay the source of
truth: the event never carries the new state, it only says "this changed,
reload it".

Design notes
------------
* **Broadcast, never targeted.** :class:`~codx.junior.sio.session_channel.SessionChannel`
  appends to ``EVENT_QUEUE``, which the background thread emits with
  ``sio.emit(event, data)`` — no ``sid`` — so the change reaches every client.
  A collection is global state, so a per-session channel would leave the other
  clients stale.
* **Best effort, never raises.** Emitting happens *after* the write succeeded.
  A lost notification degrades to the previous behaviour (a stale list until
  the next reload) and must never turn a successful save into an error. Every
  failure is logged and swallowed.
* **Called from the managers, not the routers.** ``ProfileManager``,
  ``TeamManager``, ``ChatManager`` and :func:`create_project` are the choke
  points shared by the REST API, the AI tools and the background workers, so a
  profile created by ``profile_management`` reaches the clients exactly like
  one created through ``POST /api/profiles``.

Diagram
-------
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Save[ProfileManager / TeamManager / ChatManager / create_project] --> Emit[emit_collection_event]
    Emit --> Queue[SessionChannel EVENT_QUEUE]
    Queue --> Sio[socket.io broadcast]
    Sio --> Clients[Clients: codx-junior-collection]
    Clients --> Store[store/collections.js reloads that collection]
```

def _action_list_tasks(
    chat_manager,
    board: Optional[str] = None,
    column: Optional[str] = None,
    sprint: Optional[str] = None,
    status: Optional[str] = None,
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List the project's tasks with optional filters.

    Filters are not validated on purpose: filtering by a board/column/state that
    does not exist simply returns no tasks, which is a harmless way to discover
    that the destination is missing.

    Args:
        chat_manager: The project ChatManager.
        board: Only tasks on this board.
        column: Only tasks on this column.
        sprint: Only tasks associated to this sprint.
        status: Only tasks with this status (case-insensitive).
        query: Case-insensitive substring matched against name and description.
        limit: Maximum number of tasks returned.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with a Markdown table (user) and JSON (model).
    """
    chats = chat_manager.list_chats()

    if board:
        chats = [c for c in chats if (c.board or "").lower() == board.lower()]
    if column:
        chats = [c for c in chats if (c.column or "").lower() == column.lower()]
    if sprint:
        chats = [c for c in chats if sprint in (c.sprints or [])]
    if status:
        chats = [c for c in chats if (c.status or "").lower() == status.lower()]
    if query:
        needle = query.strip().lower()
        chats = [
            c for c in chats
            if needle in (c.name or "").lower()
            or needle in (c.description or "").lower()
        ]

    chats = sorted(chats, key=lambda c: str(c.updated_at or ""), reverse=True)
    total = len(chats)
    if limit and limit > 0:
        chats = chats[:limit]

    if not chats:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="✓ No tasks match the given filters.",
            llm_response=_json({"count": 0, "tasks": []}),
        )

    lines = [
        f"> {len(chats)} of {total} task(s)",
        "",
        "**ID** | **Name** | **Status** | **Board/Column** | **Sprints** | **Updated**",
        "---|---|---|---|---|---",
    ]
    for chat in chats:
        sprints = ", ".join(chat.sprints or []) or "-"
        name = (chat.name or "(unnamed)").replace("|", "/")
        lines.append(
            f"`{_short_id(chat)}` | {name} | {chat.status or '-'} | "
            f"{chat.board}/{chat.column} | {sprints} | {chat.updated_at}"
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(lines),
        llm_response=_json({"count": len(chats), "total": total, "tasks": [
            _task_dict(chat) for chat in chats
        ]}),
    )

"""
Task archiving: compress finished tasks instead of keeping every chat live.

Problem solved
--------------
``.codx/tasks`` only grows: each turn appends messages to one JSON file and
nothing ever removes a task, so a busy project easily reaches hundreds of
megabytes. Every listing (``ChatManager.list_chats``, ``/api/chats``, the board
view, ``search_tasks``) then parses **all** of those files, and the board gets
buried under tasks nobody will open again.

Archiving takes one task out of the live tree and stores it compressed:

* the task disappears from every listing, search, cost roll-up and board,
  because :meth:`ChatManager.chat_paths` only discovers real chat files,
* it occupies a fraction of the space (gzip on an indented JSON chat is
  typically 10-20x smaller),
* it can be restored later, byte for byte, into the same board/column.

Layout
------
::

    .codx/tasks/
      <board>/<column>/<slug>.<chat_id>.json   live tasks
      .archive/
        index.json                             catalogue (metadata only)
        <chat_id>.tar.gz                       the archived task (chat.json)
        .archive.lock                          cross process write lock

``.archive`` lives **inside** ``tasks`` on purpose: archiving never crosses a
filesystem, and the project stays self contained (copy the ``.codx`` folder and
the archived tasks travel with it). The folder is hidden and excluded from chat
discovery by :func:`codx.junior.kanban.model.is_store_file`.

Why a tar.gz and not a single gzip
----------------------------------
A ``tar.gz`` keeps the original **file name** inside the archive. Restoring the
task therefore needs no guessing: the extracted name is the same
``<slug>.<chat_id>.json`` the chat manager produced, so a restored task is
indistinguishable from one that was never archived.

Index vs. payload
-----------------
``index.json`` holds only the metadata needed to *list* an archived task
(name, board, column, status, dates, sizes...). Listing archived tasks never
opens a payload, which is what makes ``include_archived=true`` cheap even with
thousands of archived tasks.

Concurrency
-----------
Every mutation happens while holding an ``fcntl`` lock (the same approach the
kanban store uses), so the API process and the background worker can archive
and restore concurrently without losing an index entry. Index writes are atomic
(``tmp`` + ``os.replace``), and a partially written payload never replaces a
finished one.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import tarfile

from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional

try:  # POSIX only; the container always has it.
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - non POSIX fallback
    fcntl = None

from codx.junior.kanban.model import (
    ARCHIVE_DIR,
    ARCHIVE_INDEX_FILE,
    ARCHIVE_LOCK_FILE,
    ARCHIVE_SUFFIX,
    ARCHIVE_VERSION,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Chat files the archiver is allowed to pack (a chat is always JSON/YAML).
CHAT_SUFFIXES = (".json", ".yaml")


def chat_id_from_filename(file_path: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Extract the chat id from a chat file name.

    Chat files are always ``<slugified name>.<chat_id>.json`` (see
    :meth:`codx.junior.chat_manager.ChatManager.get_chat_file`), so the id is
    the last dot separated token, validated as a UUID.

    Args:
        file_path: Path (or file name) of a chat file.

    Returns:
        The chat id, or None when the name does not follow the convention.

    Example:
        >>> chat_id_from_filename("tasks/To do/fix-login.6f1c2b90-6d0a-4a2b-9c11-2f8d7e5a3b10.json")
        '6f1c2b90-6d0a-4a2b-9c11-2f8d7e5a3b10'
    """
    name = os.path.basename(str(file_path or ""))
    for suffix in CHAT_SUFFIXES:
        if name.endswith(suffix):
            name = name[: -len(suffix)]
            break
    parts = name.split(".")
    if len(parts) < 2:
        return None
    candidate = parts[-1]
    if len(candidate) == 36 and candidate.count("-") == 4:
        return candidate
    return None


class TaskArchive:
    """
    Compressed storage of archived tasks of one project.

    Attributes:
        tasks_path: Absolute ``<codx_path>/tasks`` folder.
        archive_path: Absolute ``<tasks>/.archive`` folder.
    """

    def __init__(self, tasks_path: str) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            tasks_path: Absolute path of the project's ``tasks`` folder.
        """
        self.tasks_path = os.path.abspath(str(tasks_path))
        self.archive_path = os.path.join(self.tasks_path, ARCHIVE_DIR)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Paths
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def index_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the archive catalogue."""
        return os.path.join(self.archive_path, ARCHIVE_INDEX_FILE)

    @property
    def lock_file(self) -> str:
        """Absolute path of the archive write lock."""
        return os.path.join(self.archive_path, ARCHIVE_LOCK_FILE)

    def archive_file(self, chat_id: str) -> str:
        """
        Absolute path of the payload of *chat_id*.

        Args:
            chat_id: Id of the archived task.

        Returns:
            Path of the ``<chat_id>.tar.gz`` file.
        """
        return os.path.join(self.archive_path, f"{chat_id}{ARCHIVE_SUFFIX}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Low level IO
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    @contextmanager
    def locked(self) -> Iterator[None]:
        """
        Hold the archive lock (cross process).

        Serialises archiving and restoring between the API process and the
        background worker. Degrades to a no-op when ``fcntl`` is unavailable.
        """
        os.makedirs(self.archive_path, exist_ok=True)
        handle = open(self.lock_file, "a+", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:
                fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            yield
        finally:
            try:
                if fcntl is not None:
                    fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
            finally:
                handle.close()

    def _read_index(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Read the catalogue, returning an empty one when missing or broken."""
        if not os.path.isfile(self.index_file):
            return {"version": ARCHIVE_VERSION, "tasks": {}}
        try:
            with open(self.index_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                data = json.loads(handle.read())
        except (OSError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.warning("archive: cannot read '%s': %s", self.index_file, ex)
            return {"version": ARCHIVE_VERSION, "tasks": {}}
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            return {"version": ARCHIVE_VERSION, "tasks": {}}
        if not isinstance(data.get("tasks"), dict):
            data["tasks"] = {}
        data.setdefault("version", ARCHIVE_VERSION)
        return data

    def _write_index(self, data: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Write the catalogue atomically so a crash never truncates it."""
        os.makedirs(self.archive_path, exist_ok=True)
        tmp_file = f"{self.index_file}.tmp"
        with open(tmp_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
        os.replace(tmp_file, self.index_file)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reading
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def entries(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return every archived task, indexed by chat id.

        Returns:
            ``{chat_id: entry}`` copied from the catalogue.
        """
        return dict(self._read_index().get("tasks") or {})

    def list_entries(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the archived tasks, most recently archived first.

        Returns:
            List of catalogue entries (metadata only, no chat content).
        """
        entries = list(self.entries().values())
        return sorted(entries, key=lambda entry: str(entry.get("archived_at") or ""), reverse=True)

    def get(self, chat_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the catalogue entry of one archived task.

        Args:
            chat_id: Id of the task.

        Returns:
            The entry, or None when the task is not archived.
        """
        return self.entries().get(str(chat_id or "").strip())

    def is_archived(self, chat_id: str) -> bool:
        """
        Tell whether a task is archived.

        Args:
            chat_id: Id of the task.

        Returns:
            True when the catalogue knows the task.
        """
        return self.get(chat_id) is not None

    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Summarise the archive (count and space saved).

        Returns:
            ``{"count", "archived_bytes", "original_bytes", "saved_bytes",
            "ratio"}`` where ``ratio`` is ``original_bytes / archived_bytes``.

        Example:
            >>> TaskArchive("/proj/.codx/tasks").stats()["count"]
            3
        """
        entries = self.entries().values()
        archived_bytes = sum(int(entry.get("size") or 0) for entry in entries)
        original_bytes = sum(int(entry.get("original_size") or 0) for entry in entries)
        return {
            "count": len(self.entries()),
            "archived_bytes": archived_bytes,
            "original_bytes": original_bytes,
            "saved_bytes": max(0, original_bytes - archived_bytes),
            "ratio": round(original_bytes / archived_bytes, 1) if archived_bytes else 0,
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Writing
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _compress(self, chat_file: str, target_file: str) -> int:
        """
        Pack *chat_file* into *target_file* as a single member ``tar.gz``.

        The member keeps the original file name so a restore needs no guessing.
        The payload is written to a ``.tmp`` file first and moved into place, so
        an interrupted compression never leaves a corrupt archive behind.

        Args:
            chat_file: Chat file to compress.
            target_file: Destination ``.tar.gz`` path.

        Returns:
            Size in bytes of the written archive.
        """
        tmp_file = f"{target_file}.tmp"
        info = tarfile.TarInfo(name=os.path.basename(chat_file))
        info.size = os.path.getsize(chat_file)
        info.mtime = int(os.path.getmtime(chat_file))
        info.mode = 0o644
        with open(chat_file, "rb") as source, tarfile.open(tmp_file, "w:gz") as tar:
            tar.addfile(info, source)
        os.replace(tmp_file, target_file)
        return os.path.getsize(target_file)

    def _extract(self, archive_file: str, target_dir: str) -> str:
        """
        Extract the single member of *archive_file* into *target_dir*.

        The member name is reduced with ``os.path.basename`` and the resulting
        path is verified to stay directly inside *target_dir*, so a crafted
        archive can never write outside the tasks tree.

        Args:
            archive_file: Path of the ``.tar.gz`` payload.
            target_dir: Folder that receives the chat file.

        Returns:
            Absolute path of the extracted chat file.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When the archive is empty, is not a chat file, or tries
                to escape *target_dir*.
        """
        target_root = os.path.abspath(target_dir)
        os.makedirs(target_root, exist_ok=True)
        with tarfile.open(archive_file, "r:gz") as tar:
            member = tar.next()
            if member is None or not member.isfile():
                raise ValueError(f"'{archive_file}' does not contain a chat file")
            name = os.path.basename(member.name)
            if not name.lower().endswith(CHAT_SUFFIXES):
                raise ValueError(f"'{archive_file}' does not contain a chat file ('{name}')")
            target_file = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(target_root, name))
            if os.path.dirname(target_file) != target_root:
                raise ValueError(f"refusing to extract '{name}' outside '{target_root}'")
            source = tar.extractfile(member)
            if source is None:
                raise ValueError(f"cannot read the chat file of '{archive_file}'")
            with open(target_file, "wb") as out:
                out.write(source.read())
        return target_file

    def archive(
        self,
        chat_file: str,
        chat_id: Optional[str] = None,
        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        archived_by: Optional[str] = None,
        original_path: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Compress a chat file and remove it from the live tree.

        The operation is idempotent: archiving an already archived task returns
        the stored entry instead of failing (the file is already gone).

        Args:
            chat_file: Absolute path of the chat file to archive.
            chat_id: Id of the chat; derived from the file name when omitted.
            metadata: Listing metadata stored in the catalogue (name, board,
                column, status, dates...). Only identifying/listing values:
                the payload already holds everything else.
            archived_by: User or profile that archived the task.
            original_path: Path relative to the tasks folder, kept for traces.

        Returns:
            The catalogue entry written for the task.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: When *chat_file* does not exist.
            ValueError: When the chat id cannot be resolved.

        Example:
            >>> TaskArchive("/proj/.codx/tasks").archive(
            ...     "/proj/.codx/tasks/Bugs/To do/fix-login.<uuid>.json",
            ...     metadata={"board": "Bugs", "column": "To do"},
            ... )
        """
        chat_file = os.path.abspath(str(chat_file or ""))
        chat_id = (chat_id or chat_id_from_filename(chat_file) or "").strip()
        if not chat_id:
            raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve the chat id of '{chat_file}'")
        if not os.path.isfile(chat_file):
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"chat file not found: '{chat_file}'")

        with self.locked():
            index = self._read_index()
            entries = index.setdefault("tasks", {})
            stored = entries.get(chat_id)
            if stored is not None:
                # Already archived (a retry, or two clients racing): keep the
                # stored entry and drop the stray live file.
                if os.path.isfile(chat_file):
                    os.remove(chat_file)
                return dict(stored)

            target_file = self.archive_file(chat_id)
            original_size = os.path.getsize(chat_file)
            size = self._compress(chat_file, target_file)
            os.remove(chat_file)

            relative = os.path.relpath(chat_file, self.tasks_path)
            entry = {
                "chat_id": chat_id,
                "archive_file": os.path.basename(target_file),
                "original_file": original_path or relative,
                "archived_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "archived_by": archived_by,
                "size": size,
                "original_size": original_size,
                **{key: value for key, value in (metadata or {}).items() if value is not None},
            }
            entries[chat_id] = entry
            self._write_index(index)

        logger.info(
            "archive: task '%s' archived (%d -> %d bytes, %.1fx)",
            chat_id,
            entry["original_size"],
            entry["size"],
            entry["original_size"] / entry["size"] if entry["size"] else 1,
        )
        return dict(entry)

    def restore(self, chat_id: str, target_dir: str) -> str:
        """
        Extract an archived task back into *target_dir* and drop the archive.

        Args:
            chat_id: Id of the archived task.
            target_dir: Folder that must receive the chat file (the board and
                column folders are resolved by the caller, which knows the
                catalogue).

        Returns:
            Absolute path of the restored chat file.

        Raises:
            FileNotFoundError: When the task is not archived or its payload is
                missing.
            ValueError: When the payload is not a readable chat archive.
        """
        chat_id = str(chat_id or "").strip()
        with self.locked():
            index = self._read_index()
            entries = index.setdefault("tasks", {})
            entry = entries.get(chat_id)
            if entry is None:
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"task '{chat_id}' is not archived")

            archive_file = self.archive_file(chat_id)
            if not os.path.isfile(archive_file):
                raise FileNotFoundError(
                    f"the archive payload of task '{chat_id}' is missing: '{archive_file}'"
                )
            restored_file = self._extract(archive_file, target_dir)
            os.remove(archive_file)
            entries.pop(chat_id, None)
            self._write_index(index)

        logger.info("archive: task '%s' restored to '%s'", chat_id, restored_file)
        return restored_file

    def forget(self, chat_id: str) -> bool:
        """
        Delete an archived task permanently (payload + catalogue entry).

        Args:
            chat_id: Id of the archived task.

        Returns:
            True when the task was archived and has been removed.
        """
        chat_id = str(chat_id or "").strip()
        with self.locked():
            index = self._read_index()
            entries = index.setdefault("tasks", {})
            if entries.pop(chat_id, None) is None:
                return False
            archive_file = self.archive_file(chat_id)
            if os.path.isfile(archive_file):
                try:
                    os.remove(archive_file)
                except OSError as ex:
                    logger.warning("archive: cannot remove '%s': %s", archive_file, ex)
            self._write_index(index)

        logger.info("archive: task '%s' permanently deleted", chat_id)
        return True

# Characters that can never appear in a directory name used as a folder.
_INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS = re.compile(r'[/\\\x00-\x1f]')


def safe_folder(name: str, default: str = "board") -> str:
    """
    Convert a board/column *title* into a directory name.

    The original case and spaces are preserved on purpose: existing projects
    already have folders such as ``To do`` or ``tasks``, and changing them would
    orphan every stored chat.

    Args:
        name: Board or column title.
        default: Value used when the title has no usable characters.

    Returns:
        A path separator free folder name.

    Example:
        >>> safe_folder("To do")
        'To do'
        >>> safe_folder("api/ui")
        'api-ui'
    """
    folder = _INVALID_FOLDER_CHARS.sub("-", str(name or "")).strip()
    folder = folder.strip(".").strip()
    return folder or default


def is_store_file(file_path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether *file_path* is part of the storage itself (not a chat).

    ``.codx/tasks`` holds both the chats and the catalogue, so any code that
    walks the tree for chats must skip ``index.json``, the legacy
    ``kanban.json``, everything under ``boards/`` and the ``.archive`` folder
    (which holds the compressed archived tasks and their own catalogue).

    Any hidden path (a path segment starting with ``.``) is storage too: the
    archive folder is hidden on purpose, so a task moves out of the live tree
    the moment it is archived.

    Args:
        file_path: Absolute or relative file path.

    Returns:
        True when the path belongs to the kanban storage.
    """
    base = os.path.basename(file_path)
    if base in (INDEX_FILE, LEGACY_FILE, BACKUP_FILE, LOCK_FILE):
        return True
    parts = [
        part for part in os.path.normpath(str(file_path)).split(os.sep)
        if part and part not in (os.curdir, os.pardir)
    ]
    if BOARDS_DIR in parts or ARCHIVE_DIR in parts:
        return True
    return any(part.startswith(".") for part in parts)


def clean_profiles(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize the ``profiles`` a board column hands to its new tasks.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Leading ``@``
    are stripped, blanks dropped and duplicates removed.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> clean_profiles(["@backend", "backend", " ui ", None])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        items = list(value)
    except TypeError:
        return []

    names: List[str] = []
    for item in items:
        clean = str(item or "").lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names

        if v > MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"Attachment size exceeds maximum allowed size of {MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB}MB")
        return v
    
    @validator('file_type')
    def validate_file_type(cls, v):
        # `MediaRecorder` reports the recording type together with its codec list

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Unsent drafts (message composer state)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The text a user is still typing is persisted with the chat as ONE draft
# message (``Message.unsent == True``). It survives reloads and crashes, but it
# is NOT part of the conversation: it must never be listed, summarized, sent to
# the model, broadcast as a chat message, exported or counted by analytics.
# Persistence is delegated to the owner ``ChatManager`` (the only chat store);
# the imports are lazy because ``chat_manager`` imports this module.


def _visible_messages(messages: Optional[List[Message]]) -> List[Message]:
    """
    Return only the messages that belong to the conversation.

    Unsent drafts (``Message.unsent``) are filtered out here, so every reader
    that goes through this helper is draft-free by construction.

    :param messages: Message list of a chat (may be ``None``).
    :return: A new list without the unsent drafts.
    """
    return [message for message in (messages or []) if not message.unsent]


def _find_unsent_message(chat: "Chat") -> Optional[Message]:
    """
    Return the unsent draft of *chat* (the most recent one when legacy data has
    more than one), or ``None`` when the chat has no draft.

    :param chat: Chat to inspect.
    :return: The draft message or ``None``.
    """
    for message in reversed(chat.messages or []):
        if message.unsent:
            return message
    return None


def _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id: str, chat_manager: Any = None) -> Any:
    """
    Resolve the ``ChatManager`` that stores *chat_id*.

    The manager is injectable (``chat_manager``) because the API layer already
    holds the session manager; otherwise the projects are searched the same way
    ``/api/chats/message`` resolves a chat id.

    :param chat_id: Chat whose store is needed.
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved manager.
    :return: The manager holding the chat, or ``None`` when it is unknown.
    """
    if chat_manager is not None:
        return chat_manager

    from codx.junior.chat_manager import ChatManager
    from codx.junior.project.project_discover import find_all_projects

    try:
        projects = find_all_projects()
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.warning("draft: cannot list projects for chat '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
        return None

    for settings in projects.values():
        try:
            manager = ChatManager(settings=settings)
            if manager.find_by_id(chat_id) is not None:
                return manager
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning(
                "draft: project scan failed for chat '%s': %s", chat_id, ex
            )
    return None


def get_unsent_message(chat_id: str, chat_manager: Any = None) -> Optional[Message]:
    """
    Return the unsent draft of *chat_id*.

    Only the client composer that owns the draft should call this: the returned
    message is not part of the conversation (see :func:`_visible_messages`).

    :param chat_id: Chat whose draft is requested.
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved ``ChatManager``.
    :return: The draft message, or ``None`` when the chat has no draft.
    """
    if not chat_id:
        return None
    manager = _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id, chat_manager)
    chat = manager.find_by_id(chat_id) if manager else None
    if chat is None:
        return None
    return _find_unsent_message(chat)


def upsert_unsent_message(
    chat_id: str,
    content: str,
    author: Optional[str] = None,
    chat_manager: Any = None,
) -> Message:
    """
    Create or replace the single unsent draft of *chat_id*.

    The existing draft ``doc_id`` is reused when updating, so the client keeps
    a stable key while typing. The chat keeps at most ONE unsent message.

    :param chat_id: Chat owning the draft.
    :param content: Current composer text.
    :param author: Optional username of the composer (stored in ``Message.user``).
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved ``ChatManager``.
    :return: The persisted draft message.
    :raises ValueError: When *chat_id* is missing or unknown.
    """
    if not chat_id:
        raise ValueError("upsert_unsent_message requires a chat_id")

    manager = _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id, chat_manager)
    chat = manager.find_by_id(chat_id) if manager else None
    if chat is None:
        raise ValueError(f"upsert_unsent_message: chat '{chat_id}' not found")

    message = _find_unsent_message(chat)
    if message is None:
        message = Message(
            doc_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
            role=ROLE_USER,
            content=content or '',
            user=author,
            unsent=True,
        )
        manager.add_message(chat=chat, message=message)
        return message

    message.role = ROLE_USER
    message.content = content or ''
    message.unsent = True
    if author is not None:
        message.user = author
    manager.update_message(chat=chat, message=message)
    return message


def delete_unsent_message(chat_id: str, chat_manager: Any = None) -> bool:
    """
    Remove the unsent draft of *chat_id*.

    :param chat_id: Chat whose draft must be discarded.
    :param chat_manager: Optional already-resolved ``ChatManager``.
    :return: ``True`` when a draft was deleted, ``False`` when there was none.
    """
    if not chat_id:
        return False
    manager = _resolve_chat_manager(chat_id, chat_manager)
    chat = manager.find_by_id(chat_id) if manager else None
    if chat is None:
        return False
    message = _find_unsent_message(chat)
    if message is None:
        return False
    manager.remove_message(chat=chat, message_doc_id=message.doc_id)
    return True

"""
Chat + AI
This module is responsible for chat persistence and management.

Besides the classic full-chat ``save_chat``, this module now exposes granular,
merge-safe message operations (``add_message``, ``update_message``,
``remove_message``) used to persist chat changes *during* an AI turn (e.g.
tool-usage notification messages, streamed partial responses) without
overwriting concurrent updates.

It also provides full-text search capabilities via the ``search_chats`` method,
delegating to the ``ChatSearcher`` class for filtering by time frame, keyword
matching, and pagination.

Merge strategy (per message, keyed by ``doc_id``):

    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        A[Incoming chat messages] --> C{doc_id exists in stored chat?}
        B[Stored chat messages] --> C
        C -->|No| D[Keep message]
        C -->|Yes| E{parse incoming.updated_at >= parse stored.updated_at?}
        E -->|Yes| F[Keep incoming]
        E -->|No| G[Keep stored]
        D --> H[Merged message list]
        F --> H
        G --> H
    ```

CHANGED — kanban storage v2:
    ``load_kanban`` / ``save_kanban`` / ``delete_kanban`` delegate to
    :class:`codx.junior.kanban.store.KanbanStore`, which keeps one file per board
    behind an ``fcntl`` lock and migrates the legacy single ``kanban.json``.
    Board/column **folders are immutable**: :meth:`ChatManager.get_chat_file`
    resolves the folder from the catalogue (``resolve_folders``) instead of
    using ``Chat.board``/``Chat.column`` directly, so renaming a board no longer
    moves a folder nor rewrites every task.

CHANGED — chat file discovery:
    :meth:`ChatManager.chat_paths` only returns real chat files
    (``<board>/<column>/<name>.<id>.json``). The storage files (``index.json``,
    ``kanban.json``, ``boards/<id>/board.json``) live in the same tree and must
    never be parsed as chats.

CHANGED — exact chat lookup:
    :meth:`ChatManager.find_by_id` matches the ``.<chat_id>.json`` suffix
    instead of ``chat_id in path``. The substring match returned the wrong chat
    whenever two ids shared a prefix, which broke ancestor resolution.

CHANGED — timestamp normalisation:
    ``updated_at`` values historically exist in TWO formats:
    ``str(datetime.now())`` (space separator, Message default) and
    ``datetime.isoformat()`` (T separator, stamped by add/update_message).
    Comparing them as raw strings is WRONG ("...T..." always beats "... ..."
    lexicographically for the same day). :func:`_parse_timestamp` parses both
    formats so the last-writer-wins decision uses real datetimes.

CHANGED — persist hot-path:
    The granular operations are now called frequently mid-run (tool events,
    throttled stream persists). :meth:`ChatManager._load_stored_chat` reads
    the chat directly from ``chat.file_path`` when possible instead of
    scanning the whole tasks tree via ``find_by_id``.

NEW — chat search:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.search_chats` method provides full-text search
    across all chat data with optional time-frame filtering, user filtering,
    and pagination, delegating to :class:`codx.junior.chat_searcher.ChatSearcher`.

NEW — chat filtering:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.get_recent_chats` method now supports filtering by
    user_id, board, column, and chat_type (task or chat).

CHANGED — project_ids filtering:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.search_chats` method now supports filtering by
    project_ids list. When no query is provided, returns latest chats from
    accessible user projects.

CHANGED — chat ID validation:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.load_chat_from_path` method now ensures all loaded
    chats have a valid ID. Missing IDs are extracted from the filename or
    generated fresh, guaranteeing no chat is returned without an ID.

CHANGED — time-range filtering:
    :meth:`ChatManager.chat_paths` and :meth:`ChatManager.list_chats` now
    accept an optional **upper bound** (``before_update`` / ``to_date``) in
    addition to the existing lower bound (``last_update`` / ``from_date``),
    enabling an explicit ``[from_date, to_date]`` window. Both bounds are
    applied against the chat file ``mtime``. When a bound is ``None`` it is
    ignored, so existing callers are unaffected.

NEW — accumulated chat cost (``Chat.cost``):
    ``Chat.cost`` accumulates the cxjcoins spent on a chat. It is updated here
    whenever a message carrying a cost is added or updated, using the persisted
    version of that message as the baseline (so a cost registered *after* the
    message was first persisted is still captured exactly once). The value is
    MONOTONIC — deleting a message never reduces it — so the chat budget stays
    accurate even when messages are removed.

NEW — cost roll-up to the root chat:
    The same delta is also added to the **root** chat of the tree
    (``Chat.root_id``, see :mod:`codx.junior.identity`). That makes the budget
    of a main task (``Chat.estimation_cost``) cover every descendant turn, which
    is what a long-running run needs: the run budget lives on the main task and
    the agent already stops a turn when ``Chat.cost`` reaches
    ``Chat.estimation_cost``.

NEW — chat status history (``Chat.status_history``):
    ``Chat.status`` was previously a single mutable field ("last writer wins"),
    making it impossible to reconstruct when a task moved between statuses. This
    module now appends a :class:`codx.junior.db.ChatStatusEvent` to
    ``Chat.status_history`` every time ``status`` actually changes (detected in
    :meth:`ChatManager.save_chat` via :meth:`ChatManager._register_status_change`).
    The log is append-only and merge-safe (dedup by ``doc_id``), giving future
    task-performance metrics (cycle time, throughput, error rate) the raw
    transition feed they need.
"""
